data.title: Google suffers data breach in ongoing Salesforce data theft attacks
data.author: mikece
data.article_summary: Google近日证实，在今年6月成为ShinyHunters黑客组织针对Salesforce客户关系管理（CRM）系统数据盗窃攻击的受害者。攻击者通过语音钓鱼（vishing）诈骗获取员工信息，入侵Salesforce实例并窃取客户数据，试图勒索公司支付赎金以防止数据泄露。被盗数据包括中小企业的基础联系信息，多为公开可获取的数据。ShinyHunters已进行多次类似攻击，目标包括Adidas、Qantas、Cisco等公司，部分公司已支付赎金以避免数据泄露。攻击者还计划在私下的勒索结束后，将数据公开或在黑客论坛上出售。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google使用Salesforce系统时发生数据泄露事件，参与者讨论了数据泄露的原因、影响以及Google为何使用第三方客户管理系统而非自建系统。

不同观点：
• [kyrra & GHanku] 引用的文章指出，数据泄露涉及威胁行为者通过Salesforce Data Loader获取中小企业联系信息和相关笔记。泄露的数据包括基本的公开业务信息，如企业名称和联系方式。GHanku进一步解释了攻击者如何通过社会工程学手段，诱骗员工连接到恶意的Data Loader应用以导出数据，并利用这些数据访问其他云平台。

• [cjonas] 猜测泄露可能源于force.com网站的配置错误，这种配置错误允许公开访问基本业务信息。他提到这种问题在过去很常见，尽管Salesforce已经发布了许多安全补丁，但大多需要管理员手动操作才能生效。他还指出，这种漏洞广泛存在，但奇怪的是没有引起媒体关注。

• [Bluescreenbuddy & grumple] 对Google为何不开发自己的内部客户管理系统表示惊讶，认为Google似乎没有销售人员或客户管理需求，使用Salesforce显得不寻常。

• [ok123456] 提出了此次事件是否与AI生成内容有关的猜测，链接了一篇关于AI撰写销售材料的文章，但未展开讨论具体关联。

• [wferrell] 解释了Google内部CRM系统存在的问题，指出其有缺陷且工程师不愿意维护，暗示使用Salesforce可能是出于无奈。

• [mrweasel] 联想到自己经历的数据丢失事件，怀疑是否与KLM的数据泄露有关，但未提供具体证据。

• [shadowgovt] 对Google使用Salesforce表示理解，指出Google通过收购快速扩展，可能继承了被收购公司的系统。他还提到Google内部对开发Salesforce替代品的兴趣不大，因为员工认为这样的工作枯燥乏味。

• [01HNNWZ0MV43FF] 简短地评论了数据泄露事件的影响，指出最终受害者是用户，并用幽默链接了一首歌曲。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对Salesforce配置错误导致数据泄露的技术细节，以及Google为何选择使用第三方系统而非自建系统的原因分析。
• 参与者还提到了攻击者如何利用社会工程学手段获取数据，以及Google内部CRM系统存在的缺陷和工程师对维护这些系统的抵触情绪。
• 争议的焦点在于Google这样的大公司为何依赖第三方客户管理系统，以及在数据安全和系统维护上的责任归属。

44812198.article_content:
Google suffers data breach in ongoing Salesforce data theft attacks
By
Lawrence Abrams
August 6, 2025
09:51 AM
0
Google is the latest company to suffer a data breach in an ongoing wave of Salesforce CRM data theft attacks conducted by the ShinyHunters extortion group.
In June,
Google warned
that a threat actor they classify as 'UNC6040' is targeting companies' employees in voice phishing (vishing) social engineering attacks to breach Salesforce instances and download customer data. This data is then used to extort companies into paying a ransom to prevent the data from being leaked.
In a brief update to the article last night, Google said that it too fell victim to the same attack in June after one of its Salesforce CRM instances was breached and customer data was stolen.
"In June, one of Google's corporate Salesforce instances was impacted by similar UNC6040 activity described in this post. Google responded to the activity, performed an impact analysis and began mitigations,"
reads Google's update
.
"The instance was used to store contact information and related notes for small and medium businesses. Analysis revealed that data was retrieved by the threat actor during a small window of time before the access was cut off."
"The data retrieved by the threat actor was confined to basic and largely publicly available business information, such as business names and contact details."
Google is classifying the threat actors behind these attacks as 'UNC6040' or 'UNC6240.' However, BleepingComputer, which has been tracking these attacks, has learned that a notorious threat actor known as
ShinyHunters is behind the attacks
.
ShinyHunters has been around for years, responsible for a wide range of breaches, including those at
PowerSchool
,
Oracle Cloud
, the
Snowflake data-theft attacks
,
AT&T
,
NitroPDF
,
Wattpad
,
MathWay
, and
many more
.
In a conversation with BleepingComputer yesterday, ShinyHunters claimed to have breached many Salesforce instances, with attacks still ongoing.
The threat actor claimed yesterday to BleepingComputer that they breached a trillion-dollar company, and were considering just leaking the data rather than attempting to extort them. It is unclear if this company is Google.
As for the other companies impacted in these attacks, the threat actor is extorting them through email, demanding they pay a ransom to prevent the data from being publicly leaked.
Once the threat actor has finished privately extorting companies, they plan to publicly leak or sell data on a hacking forum.
BleepingComputer has learned of one company that has already paid 4 Bitcoins, or approximately $400,000, to prevent the leak of their data.
Other companies impacted in these attacks include
Adidas
,
Qantas
,
Allianz Life
,
Cisco
, and the LVMH subsidiaries
Louis Vuitton
,
Dior
, and
Tiffany & Co.

data.title: The Inkhaven Blogging Residency
data.author: venkii
data.article_summary: 《INKHAVEN写作营》是一项为期一个月的驻留项目，将于11月1日至30日在加州伯克利举行。该项目招收约30人，参与者需每天撰写并发布一篇博客文章，否则将被要求离开。项目费用为3500美元（包括住宿），并提供奖学金。知名顾问包括Scott Alexander、Scott Aaronson和Gwern，组织者为Ben Pace、Oliver Habryka和Lightcone Infrastructure。申请结果将在10天内通知。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对写作静修营（residency）的性质、费用、价值以及相关商业模式的讨论。

不同观点：
• **质疑费用与价值**：[tty456] 认为花费3500美元只是为了在一个类似宿舍的地方写作，不值得称为“驻留项目”（residency）。这种高额费用让人质疑其真正的价值。

• **项目组织者回应**：[habryka] 作为项目组织者之一，出面澄清并表示愿意回答任何相关问题，表明项目还涉及运营其他平台（如LessWrong.com），并暗示该项目可能有更多背景和细节。

• **定义争议：静修 vs. 驻留**：[ttoinou] 提出该项目更像是一个“静修”（retreat）而不是“驻留项目”，并询问如何找到更多类似的活动，尤其是欧洲的类似活动。这引发了对“驻留项目”定义的讨论。

• **经济能力与机会不平等**：[egypturnash] 表达了对高额费用的无奈，认为自己无法负担这样的费用，尽管承认这样的环境可能有助于创作。这反映了机会不平等和经济能力对参与这种项目的影响。

• **机构建设视角**：[ajkjk] 从更广泛的社会视角看待这个项目，认为这是千禧一代在尝试“机构建设”，暗示该项目可能具有更长远的社会意义。

• **AI写作工具对比**：[miohtama] 提到AI写作工具的费用仅为20美元/月，暗示这样的写作项目费用过高，可能不具备性价比。

• **对写作成果的兴趣**：[cosmicgadget] 表示对参与者写作成果的兴趣，希望看到这些参加者在项目中的写作表现。

• **远程参与的可能性**：[tenkabuto] 提到希望以较低成本远程参与类似活动，并建议建立一个聚合博客文章的平台，以便从外部关注该项目。

• **商业模式的讨论**：[netown] 将该项目比作“博客领域的Y-Combinator”，但指出其商业模式的不同——参与者需要提前支付费用，而不是由“提供者”进行长期投资。这引发了对该模式是否可持续和有效的讨论。

• **意识形态的隐含性**：[benwerd] 认为该项目背后有未明言的意识形态，主要围绕LessWrong社区。他提出是否可以有一个更人文主义版本的项目。

• **历史对比**：[defrost] 通过引用Inklings的历史（如C.S. Lewis的圈子），指出过去的文学讨论成本低廉，暗示现代写作项目的高费用可能不必要。

• **幽默讽刺**：[tolerance] 和 [TimorousBestie] 以幽默和讽刺的方式评论项目的名称和参与者组合，暗示项目的名称和参与者的搭配有些不协调。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到费用问题，反映出高额费用对不同人群的影响以及对项目价值的质疑。
• 对“驻留项目”定义的争议引发了关于静修与驻留项目区别的讨论。
• 商业模式和意识形态的讨论揭示了项目背后的结构性问题以及可能的社会文化背景。

data.title: Git-fetch-file – Sync files from other repos with commit tracking and safety
data.author: andrewmcwatters
data.article_summary: `git-fetch-file` 是一个可以从其他 Git 仓库中获取和同步单个文件或文件集的工具，具有提交跟踪和本地更改保护功能。它类似于一个简化的子模块，但仅针对你想要的文件。主要功能包括：从远程仓库拉取单个文件或文件集，通过 `.git-remote-files` 文件记录来源和提交信息，支持强制覆盖本地更改和更新跟踪的提交。它提供简单的命令行接口，可以通过 Git 别名或直接保存到 PATH 进行安装。主要命令包括 `add`（跟踪文件）、`pull`（下载跟踪文件）和 `status`（查看跟踪文件状态）。该工具采用 GPL-2.0 许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[如何高效地从不同代码库中提取并跟踪文件]

不同观点：
• [支持使用新工具git-remote-files]  
  - 用户andrewmcwatters提出git-remote-files工具，可以单独跟踪并更新其他仓库的特定文件，避免使用笨重的submodules或拉取过多文件。  
  - 用户ttoinou认为该工具优于git submodules，因为后者只能跟踪commit ID，不够灵活。  
  - 用户dpsych表示这正是他需要的解决方案。  

• [考虑替代方案]  
  - 用户neomantra提到使用CI脚本校验文件checksum的方案，认为这是一种轻量级的通用解决方法，避免了submodules的复杂性。  

• [实际问题驱动讨论]  
  - 用户Bukhmanizer提出从不同仓库拼接复杂软件的艺术项目设想，引发对文件提取工具的讨论。  
  - 用户neomantra和andrewmcwatters均提到实际开发中需要从上游仓库提取文件的场景，但依赖管理或submodules无法满足需求。  

补充讨论：  
- 争议焦点在于如何平衡灵活性与可靠性：submodules虽稳定但笨重，新工具更灵活但可能引入信任问题（如neomantra对二进制文件来源的担忧）。  
- andrewmcwatters后续补充了分支跟踪和.gitignore集成功能，进一步优化方案。

git-fetch-file
Fetch and sync individual files or globs from other Git repositories, with commit tracking and local-change protection
git-fetch-file(1)
is a utility for importing specific files from other Git repositories into your own project while keeping a manifest (.git-remote-files) that remembers where they came from and what commit they belong to.
It’s like a mini submodule, but for just the files you want.
Features
Pull a single file or glob from a remote Git repo
Track origin, commit, and comments in .git-remote-files
Optionally overwrite local changes with
--force
Update tracked commits with
--save
Simple CLI interface
Installation
Option 1: Git Alias (Recommended)
Save the script anywhere and set up a Git alias:
git config --global alias.fetch-file
'
!python3 /path/to/git-fetch-file.py
'
Then run it like this:
git fetch-file
<
subcommand
>
[args...]
Option 2: PATH Installation
Save the script as
git-fetch-file
somewhere on your PATH.
Commands
add
Track a file (or glob) from a remote Git repository.
git fetch-file add
<
repo
>
<
path
>
[target_dir] [--commit
<
commit
>
] [--glob] [--no-glob] [--comment
<
text
>
]
repo: The URL or path to the remote Git repo
path: Path (or glob if --glob is used) to the file(s) in the remote repo
target_dir: Optional target directory to place the file (preserves filename)
--commit: Optional commit, branch, or tag to track (default: HEAD)
--glob: If specified, interprets path as a glob pattern
--no-glob: If specified, treats path as literal filename (overrides auto-detection)
--comment: Add a descriptive comment to the manifest
pull
Download all tracked files.
git fetch-file pull [--force] [--save]
--force: Overwrite local changes to files
--save: Update the commit in .git-remote-files if you're tracking a branch or tag that moved
status
View all tracked files.
git fetch-file status
git fetch-file list
#
alias for status
.git-remote-files
Each tracked file is recorded in .git-remote-files (INI format). Example entry:
[file "lib/util.py"]
repo
= https://github.com/example/tools
commit
= a1b2c3d
target
= vendor
comment
= Common utility function
This file should be committed to your repository.
Example
Track a remote file
git fetch-file add https://github.com/user/project utils/logger.py --commit main --comment
"
Logging helper
"
Track a file into a specific directory
git fetch-file add https://github.com/user/project utils/logger.py vendor --commit main --comment
"
Third-party logging helper
"
Pull it into your repo
git fetch-file pull

data.title: Why Building Billing Systems Is So Painful (2024)
data.author: Rafsark
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了构建计费系统的复杂性，尽管表面上看起来只是定期向客户收费。作者解释了不同计费模式的挑战，如订阅制（包括基础、进阶、高级套餐）、按席位收费模式，以及近年来兴起的按使用量计费模式。每种模式都带来了独特的技术难题，如处理试用期、中途升级或降级、实时使用跟踪、高吞吐量事件处理、以及灵活适应不断变化的定价模型等。

计费系统不仅仅是开具发票，它涵盖了整个收入管理流程，包括合同管理、产品供应、使用量计量、权限管理、发票生成与交付、付款处理和收入确认。因此，计费系统是企业经济命脉，其复杂性远超预期，涉及大量技术和架构挑战。

#
What is billing
Billing might seem like a straightforward concept at first glance. When I talk about billing to friends, most of them bring up their monthly subscriptions, whether it's Netflix, Spotify, ChatGPT or something similar. How hard can it be to engineer a system to support this? After all, all you need to do is to charge a customer a fixed amount each month. You can probably set up a cron job to do that. Done. However, as any seasoned engineer will tell you, the billing space is a deceptively complex beast that becomes exponentially more intricate as your product scales. Let's talk about that complexity.
So what is billing exactly? First, let's talk about subscriptions. It's a revenue management model where businesses charge recurring payments for access to products or services. A common example is the good-better-best pricing model used by many SaaS startups. Customers choose a tier (good, better, or best) and pay a flat rate for it. Typically each tier has both monthly and yearly prices. For example, Netflix offers the following 3 tiers: (1) Basic: $7.99/month, (2) Standard: $10.99/month, and (3) Premium: $13.99/month. At Stripe we put together the following diagram to
demonstrate the good-better-best approach
:
Another popular pricing model example is per-seat pricing. In this case the user picks how many seats they plan to use, and the business then charges them based on that amount (another diagram from Stripe):
Sounds easy. However, each of these models comes with its own set of challenges. From managing trial periods that need to be billed at a reduced amount or offered for free, to handling upgrades and downgrades that can happen in the middle of the billing cycle, which then prompts the additional complexity of prorated charges or credits. From managing fixed contract periods with financial penalties for early cancellation, to supporting multiple currencies once you want to sell your product globally. From allowing customers to bundle several products together at a discounted rate, to managing entitlements to grant or revoke features based on the customer's active subscription plan.
In recent years, another pricing model found itself in the limelight — usage-based billing (I blame AI). You pay exactly for the resources you consume. That could be hours of CPU usage, number of function invocations at the edge, GB of egress for storage, number of tokens generated, etc. This all sounds great, yet, all of this introduces another layer of technical challenges:
Real-time usage tracking. Real-time is the keyword here. In order to provide customers with visibility into resource consumption the billing system needs to work in real time. As your customers approach certain usage and cost thresholds, you may need to notify them, before they receive an unexpected $100,000 invoice. This typically means relying on a stateless event-based architecture, to both provide a real-time balance and scalable webhooks platform.
Handling high ingestion volume (think hundreds of thousands of events per second). The whole billing system needs to be designed to handle extremely high throughput and scale with concurrent load.
Adapting to changing pricing models. E.g., if an application developer defines a billable event as "GB used" and then decides to change it to "GB used per region", you shouldn't require the application developer to reimplement their pricing model and integration.
Allowing for flexibility in the data model. If you change packaging, pricing, or decide to add a new product, it's important not to force application developers reimplement the entire integration: they shouldn't need to create new billable metrics, make changes to integration around subscriptions, products, prices, customers, or backfill all of their previous subscriptions.
These are just a few examples. The folks over at Lago have more stories about
why billing is 100x harder than you think
. If that's not enough to convince you,
read this
.
#
Why billing matters
Billing isn't just about sending an invoice to your customer. It's the lifeblood of your business. Full stop. Simply put, if you can't charge for your product, then there isn't really any economic value from it. Billing ultimately dictates how your business makes money. Typically billing isn't just invoicing, instead it spans an entire revenue management workflow: from contract and quote management, to provisioning, from product and price management, to usage metering, from managing entitlements, to invoice generation and delivery, from payment processing, to revenue recognition. 44819968.article_content:
Model performance
How we run GPT OSS 120B at 500+ tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs
How we optimized GPT OSS 120B for state-of-the-art latency and throughput on launch day.
Authors
Amir Haghighat
Tri Dao
Abu Qader
Bryce Dubayah
Philip Kiely
Last updated
August 7, 2025
Share
TL;DR
Day zero model performance optimization work is a mix of experimentation, bug fixing, and benchmarking guided by intuition and experience. This writeup outlines the process we followed to achieve SOTA latency and throughput for GPT OSS 120B on NVIDIA GPUs at launch with the Baseten Inference Stack.
The day an open source model like OpenAI’s new gpt-oss-120b is released, we race to make the model as performant as possible for our customers. As a
launch partner
for OpenAI’s first open-source LLM since 2019, we wanted to give developers a great experience with the new LLMs.
By the end of launch day, we were the clear leader running on NVIDIA GPUs for both latency and throughput per public data from real-world use on
OpenRouter
.
✕
What matters is having the inference optimization muscle to immediately push on latency and throughput
Optimizing performance on a new model is a substantial engineering challenge. Thanks to our flexible
inference stack
and the collective expertise of our model performance engineering team, we are able to roll out performance improvements by the hour on new models.
In fact, in the time it took to write this blog post, we added another 100 tokens per second while maintaining 100% uptime.
✕
OpenRouter performance for GPT OSS, 6:45 PM August 6, 2025
Model performance efforts included:
Testing and benchmarking across inference frameworks (TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and SGLang)
Ensuring compatibility with Hopper and Blackwell GPU architectures
Integrating with key pieces of our inference stack, including NVIDIA Dynamo
Layering in our favorite performance optimizations, like KV cache-aware routing and speculative decoding with Eagle
Below are the steps we took to achieve our goal of SOTA performance with full context window support.
Step 1: Running first inference
The first step is running baseline inference however possible. Running inference on a model requires support at the inference framework, hardware architecture, and model server level.
Inspired by GPUs, we parallelized this effort across multiple engineers. One engineer tried vLLM, another SGLang, and a third worked on TensorRT-LLM. We were able to quickly get TensorRT-LLM working, which was fortunate as it is usually the most performant inference framework for LLMs.
✕
NVIDIA cut a dev release of TensorRT-LLM to support GPT OSS
With TensorRT-LLM, it was important to serve the model on both Hopper and Blackwell architectures to support widely-available H100 GPUs and access the speed of B200 GPUs for our public model APIs.
One key tenet of the Baseten Inference Runtime is flexibility. This is especially useful when serving new models with novel architectures. Navigating, and when necessary updating, the support matrix across the entire stack requires the ability to swap between tools quickly.
Step 2: Fixing compatibility bugs
Whenever a new model architecture is released, there will be subtle bugs and issues when integrating it into existing frameworks. The GPT OSS release added multiple new technologies, including
Harmony
, a new response format.
✕
Romain Huet of OpenAI warns that implementation details affect performance and output quality.
A large part of our engineering work was iteratively fixing bugs and testing models for both speed and correctness. Where we could, we
contributed back to open source
with the fixes that worked for us.
Thanks to the hard work of open source maintainers worldwide, there are multiple excellent options for running GPT OSS, and bugs are getting identified and fixed quickly.
Step 3: Optimizing model configuration
While OpenAI advertises that GPT OSS 120B can be run on a single H100 GPU, optimized deployments parallelize the model across 4 or 8 GPUs for improved performance and throughput. There are two parallelism approaches worth considering for this model: Tensor Parallelism and Expert Parallelism.
✕
Tensor Parallelism vs Expert Parallelism for mixture of experts models
We found that Tensor Parallelism offered better latency, while Expert Parallelism offered better system throughput. As we are prioritizing latency, we selected Tensor Parallelism.
Additionally, we adopted the TensorRT-LLM MoE Backend, which is supported on Blackwell but not Hopper. This backend adds improved CUDA kernels that outperform the previous Triton backend. For more details on server configuration, see
NVIDIA’s TensorRT-LLM documentation for GPT OSS optimization
.
We packaged our preferred configuration for Hopper GPUs for the
120B
and
20B
models for dedicated deployments in our model library, and used Blackwell for our Model API.
✕
GPT OSS 120B Model API on Baseten, optimized for performance with full context window support
Next steps in performance optim

data.title: Apple announces American Manufacturing Program
data.author: Zenbit_UX
data.article_summary: 苹果公司宣布将美国投资承诺增加至6000亿美元，并推出“美国制造计划”（American Manufacturing Program, AMP）。该计划旨在将更多供应链和先进制造转移至美国，与包括Corning、Texas Instruments等在内的多家公司合作，推动关键零部件在美国生产。苹果计划未来四年在美国直接雇佣20,000人，主要集中在研发、硅工程、软件开发以及人工智能领域。此外，苹果还扩展了与Corning的合作，将在肯塔基州建立全球最大智能手机玻璃生产线，所有iPhone和Apple Watch将使用该地生产的玻璃。同时，苹果正与台积电在亚利桑那州合作生产芯片，目标在2025年生产超过190亿颗芯片，支持美国在半导体行业的领导地位。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[苹果公司对美国经济的投资承诺及其实际效果，以及Tim Cook向特朗普赠送黄金礼物的行为]

不同观点：

  - 用户列举了苹果2017、2018和2021年的多次投资承诺（如3500亿、4300亿美元），但缺乏后续实际执行证据（如njovin、xnx）。  
  - 举例Foxconn和Intel的“空头工厂”案例（insane_dreamer），认为此类声明多为公关噱头。  

• **对制造业回流的争议**  
  - 部分用户认为苹果新增就业集中在研发而非制造（insane_dreamer），且组装环节仍依赖中国（fennecfoxy）。  
  - energy123支持芯片制造回流，但反对消费电子组装回流的低效性。  

• **Tim Cook赠送黄金礼物的批评**  
  - 被讽刺为“向特朗普进贡”（Buttons840），或视为讨好威权政府的软弱行为（Arubis、cfyohyuityun）。  
  - LatteLazy则认为这只是无关实际的公关手段，类似企业迎合不同群体的象征性操作。  

• **贸易政策的争论**  
  - fennecfoxy反驳关税逻辑，指出iPhone利润主要归苹果（美国公司），关税政策无意义。  
  - Jyaif批评特朗普政策矛盾：鼓励制造业回流却迫使工程外迁。

PRESS RELEASE
August 6, 2025
Apple increases U.S. commitment to $600 billion, announces American Manufacturing Program
Apple supports more than 450,000 jobs with thousands of suppliers and partners across all 50 states — including significant expansions in Arizona, California, Iowa, Kentucky, Nevada, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Texas, and Utah
Apple increased its U.S. investment commitment to $600 billion and announced the launch of its American Manufacturing Program.
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA
Apple today announced a new $100 billion commitment to America, a significant acceleration of its U.S. investment that now totals $600 billion over the next four years. Today’s announcement includes the ambitious new American Manufacturing Program (AMP), dedicated to bringing even more of Apple’s supply chain and advanced manufacturing to the U.S. Through AMP, Apple will increase its investment across America and incentivize global companies to manufacture even more critical components in the United States.
“Today, we’re proud to increase our investments across the United States to $600 billion over four years and launch our new American Manufacturing Program,” said Tim Cook, Apple’s CEO. “This includes new and expanded work with 10 companies across America. They produce components that are used in Apple products sold all over the world, and we’re grateful to the President for his support.”
Apple parts and components manufactured in the U.S. ship to customers around the world; in fact, roughly two-thirds of the components made in the U.S. are exported to customers outside the U.S.
Today, Apple partners with thousands of suppliers across all 50 states, supporting more than 450,000 supplier and partner jobs. In the next four years, Apple plans to directly hire 20,000 people in the U.S. — the vast majority focused on R&D, silicon engineering, software development, and AI and machine learning.
Apple
American Manufacturing Program
Apple is working with its suppliers to accelerate manufacturing in the U.S. through the new American Manufacturing Program. The first AMP partners include Corning, Coherent, GlobalWafers America (GWA), Applied Materials, Texas Instruments (TI), Samsung, GlobalFoundries, Amkor, and Broadcom. This builds on
Apple’s July commitment
to buy American-made rare earth magnets from MP Materials.
The American Manufacturing Program will help fund a
major expansion of Apple’s long-standing partnership with Corning
, bringing the world’s largest and most advanced smartphone glass production line to a factory in Harrodsburg, Kentucky. The expansion means that soon, every iPhone and Apple Watch sold around the world will be built with Kentucky-made cover glass. The two companies will also open a new Apple-Corning Innovation Center in Kentucky.
Apple has also entered into a new multiyear agreement with Coherent, a long-standing partner that produces the VCSEL lasers that enable multiple features — including Face ID — on iPhone and iPad devices shipped around the world. This work takes place at Coherent’s Sherman, Texas, facility.
In July, Apple also committed to buying American-made rare earth magnets developed by MP Materials — the only fully integrated rare earth producer in the United States — significantly expanding their flagship Independence facility in Fort Worth, Texas. These magnets will become part of Apple devices shipped around the world. The two companies will also establish a cutting-edge rare earth recycling line in Mountain Pass, California.
Through its new American Manufacturing Program, Apple is working with American suppliers like Corning to accelerate U.S. manufacturing.
Through its new American Manufacturing Program, Apple is working with American suppliers like Corning to accelerate U.S. manufacturing.
Apple Expands End-to-End American Silicon Supply Chain
With these new partnerships, Apple is leading the creation of an end-to-end silicon supply chain in the United States, with partners in every key aspect of silicon production.
This U.S. silicon supply chain is on track to produce more than 19 billion chips for Apple products in 2025. That includes TSMC in Arizona, which is producing tens of millions of chips for Apple using one of the most advanced process technologies in America. Apple is this factory’s first and largest customer.
“Apple engineers work closely with suppliers across the United States to create silicon chips that are on the leading edge of innovation,” said Sabih Khan, Apple’s chief operating officer. “We’re committed to supporting U.S. suppliers involved in every key stage of the chip-making process — from the earliest stages of research and development, to final fabrication and packaging. We want America to lead in this critical industry, and we’re expanding our efforts to grow a silicon manufacturing ecosystem that will benefit innovators across America.”

data.title: FDA approves eye drops that fix near vision without glasses
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: FDA批准了一种突破性的眼药水——VIZZ，用于改善老花眼（ presbyopia ）导致的近视力模糊，无需眼镜。这种由LENZ公司开发的药水含有阿西克利定（aceclidine），每天使用一次，可在不影响远视力的情况下，提供长达10小时的清晰近视力。与早期可能导致眉毛沉重或其他副作用的眼药水不同，VIZZ通过缩小瞳孔产生“针孔效应”来改善视力，且不显著刺激眼部聚焦肌肉。该批准基于多项临床试验数据，显示其安全有效，预计2025年第四季度广泛上市。这一创新为数百万受老花眼困扰的成年人提供了新的治疗选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新型眼药水VIZZ的功效、安全性、市场前景以及与现有产品的比较。

不同观点：
• [对审批流程的质疑] merek指出FDA批准基于药企提交的试验数据，而同行评审报告通常在监管批准后发布。他对为何数据在批准后发布表示困惑。
• [个人经历与选择] FabHK提到自己在考虑LASIK/SMILE手术时，医生推荐了“单视”方案，并询问其他人是否有相关经验。
• [市场表现分析] gnatman认为Vuity（已有类似产品）市场表现不佳，可能不是因为副作用，而是因为长期使用的性价比不高。
• [产品机制与副作用] modeless和leephillips讨论了产品通过缩小瞳孔增加景深，但也指出这会减少进入眼睛的光线，可能影响视觉亮度。
• [价格与订阅模式] Mistletoe关注产品的成本，担心从一次性购买眼镜转向长期订阅眼药水。rf15也表达了对订阅模式的担忧。
• [产品适用性与剂量] pazimzadeh关心轻度老花眼的使用剂量以及过量使用的风险。amelius则提到瞳孔缩小在美观上的影响。
• [对监管机构的信任] jmclnx对FDA由于削减开支表示不信任，因此会等待多年后再考虑使用该产品。

补充讨论：
• [科幻联想] Drunk_Engineer幽默地将该产品与《星际迷航》中的Retinox5联系起来，引发了一些对未来科技的联想。
• [照明替代方案] wat10000提出是否可以通过增加照明达到类似效果，而不是依赖瞳孔缩小。

争议焦点：
• 产品发布前后的数据透明度以及为何同行评审报告在批准后发布。
• 市场对类似产品接受度低的原因是副作用还是性价比问题。
• 瞳孔缩小带来的视觉亮度降低和美观问题是否值得接受。
• 从一次性购买眼镜转向订阅眼药水的经济和实际使用影响。

FDA approves breakthrough eye drops that fix near vision without glasses
By
Bronwyn Thompson
August 06, 2025
Facebook
Twitter
Flipboard

FDA approves breakthrough eye drops that fix near vision without glasses
These new drops offer up to 10 hours of clearer vision without glasses
Depositphotos
View 1 Image
1
/
1
These new drops offer up to 10 hours of clearer vision without glasses
Depositphotos
The first aceclidine-based eye drop to improve near vision in adults with presbyopia, which affects more than 100 million adults in the US alone, has been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and will be available within three months.
Known as VIZZ, from pharmaceutical company LENZ, the drops are an aceclidine ophthalmic solution that effectively treats
presbyopia
in adults. The once-daily drops offer relief from blurry near. vision for up to 10 hours.
"The FDA approval of VIZZ is a defining moment for LENZ and represents a transformative improvement in the available treatment options for the 128 million adults living with blurry near vision in the United States," said Eef Schimmelpennink, President and Chief Executive Officer of LENZ Therapeutics. "This significant milestone is the result of tremendous commitment and collaboration by the LENZ team and our partners, the dedication of our clinical investigators, and the contributions of hundreds of participants in our clinical trials."
VIZZ works by gently shrinking the pupil of the eye, using aceclidine. This creates a “pinhole effect” – like narrowing a camera lens — which helps bring nearby objects into sharper focus. Unlike older eye drops, this one does not significantly affect the eye’s focusing muscles, so it doesn’t blur your distance vision or cause that “zoomed-in” effect (aka a myopic shift).
Ultimately, the drops offer improved reading vision for up to 10 hours, without the need for glasses and, importantly, without the side effects of older treatments.
In 2021, the very first drops to treat this condition were launched
to much acclaim, but there's a reason VIZZ drops are considered first-in-class. Vuity (pilocarpine hydrochloride 1.25%) is a dual-action eye drop that can improve near vision but may cause side effects like brow heaviness or rare vitreoretinal issues due to the ciliary muscle activation. Aceclidine, a pupil-selective miotic, works without significantly stimulating the focusing (ciliary) muscle, creating a pinhole effect – which improves near vision without adverse outcomes seen in Vuity.
"This FDA approval represents a disruptive paradigm shift in treatment options for millions of people who are frustrated and struggling with the inevitable age-related loss of their near vision," said VIZZ clinical investigator Marc Bloomenstein, from Schwartz Laser Eye Care Center in Scottsdale, Arizona. "I believe this will be a welcome solution for both optometrists and ophthalmologists who will now be able to offer a highly effective and sought-after presbyopia treatment that could immediately become the standard of care, with a product profile that will meet our patients’ needs."
The FDA approval comes on the back of three randomized, double-masked, controlled Phase II studies featuring hundreds of participants. VIZZ was well-tolerated with no serious adverse events observed in the 30,000-plus treatment days across all three trials.
Presbyopia is, unfortunately, an inevitable condition associated with aging. Almost everyone over the age of 45 experiences this near-sight vision loss, which gradually gets worse and usually requires correction with glasses or contact lenses. While presbyopia is a gradual condition, it can progress quickly and unexpectedly, making formerly simple tasks of day-to-day tasks like reading instructions or food labels more difficult.
The therapeutics company said VIZZ is expected to be broadly available in the fourth quarter of 2025, making it the first and only FDA-approved aceclidine-based eye drop for presbyopia treatment.
"This is uniquely engineered, highly-differentiated and designed to deliver quick onset and lasting benefit for the vast majority of presbyopes," said Schimmelpennink. "As we have shown, this is not only best-in-class, but frankly, the only in a class of pupil selective ciliary-sparing myotics."
The FDA approval comes based on trial data submitted by the pharmaceutical company, so it's worth noting that published peer-reviewed reports are yet to be published. Peer-reviewed publications often follow regulatory approvals, not precede them, which is common in the field of ophthalmology and dermatology.
However, the FDA data and guidance can be found
published here
.

data.title: What is the average length of a queue of cars? (2023)
data.author: alexmolas
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在山路上车辆排队长度的问题。作者最初通过概率推导，假设车辆速度独立同分布，得出每队列的平均车辆数为2。然而，经过模拟实验后，发现实际结果与此不符。模拟显示，平均队列长度约为10.69，且存在极大变异。作者最初的推导基于几何分布，但未考虑到实际情况中的复杂因素，因此得出了错误的结论。模拟结果更符合实际观察，表明队列长度分布广泛，半数队列长度不超过2，但也有长度极大的情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：车队长度和队列数量的数学模型及其推论

不同观点：
• Shawabawa3认为，如果根据上述推理，观察到一个有22,849辆车的队列几乎是不可能的。他指出，在10万辆车中总有一辆车是最慢的，当这辆车出现时，它后面的所有车都会排成一个长队。因此，平均而言，预计在后半段会有一个长达5万辆车的队列。

• Dmurray指出，结论似乎是针对错误的问题得出的：这是否是关于队列数量的公式？第一辆车以概率1开始一个队列，第二辆车只有在比第一辆车慢时（概率1/2）才开始一个新队列，第三辆车只有在比前两辆车都慢时（概率1/3）才开始一个新队列，以此类推。总和是1 + 1/2 + 1/3...，这个公式与博客文章末尾的公式一致，但存在一个错位误差。平均队列长度应为车辆总数除以这个调和数列的总和，这个和也会趋于无穷大。

• Cgadski总结了一系列独立同分布的抽样问题，并讨论了在何种情况下会抽到一个比第一次抽样更大的值。他认为，如果从绝对连续的分布中抽样，那么这个变量N会具有几何分布的特性，且其期望值为无穷大。他还提到，如果考虑有限时间内形成队列的情况，那么只有当车的速度比队列前车速度快ε时，才会加入该队列，这样就可以避免λ趋近于0的极端情况。此外，他还讨论了“体验”队列长度的问题，指出通过大量数值模拟可以发现，几乎所有司机都会遇到极大的队列。

补充讨论：
• Alexchamberlain以讽刺的方式指出，假设道路只有一个入口、没有出口，并且无限长，似乎还忘了假设道路是没有弹性和质量的。这暗示了对模型假设的质疑。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于车队长度的计算方法和假设的合理性。Shawabawa3和Dmurray对计算公式和队列数量的理解存在分歧，而Cgadski则进一步分析了不同分布假设下的结果差异，并指出了模拟与理论推导之间的矛盾。Alexchamberlain则质疑了模型假设的现实性。

44782229.article_content:
Some time ago I was driving on a twisty mountain road, stuck in a slow-moving queue of cars as it was impossible to overtake safely.
Out of boredom, I was wondering how many cars were in the queue, and, more generally, what would be the average length of queues in this road.
Let’s find out!
First, let’s formalize the problem.
Assume that the road has a single entry, no exits, and is infinitely long (poor drivers!).
Furthermore, upon entering the road each vehicle moves forward at a given average speed.
In this scenario, faster vehicles will eventually catch up with the slower ones in front of them, and, since overtakes are not possible, will slow down and queue behind them.
After some time, a “steady state” is reached where several groups of vehicles form, each moving forward at the speed of the slowest vehicle in front of the queue.
The question we want to answer is, therefore: what is the average length of these groups?
The intuitive (but wrong) approach
The first idea I had was rather intuitive, but as it turns out, wrong.
Let the average speeds of the $i$-th vehicle entering the road be $X_i$, and assume that all $X_1\ldots,X_\infty$ are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.).
Following our assumptions above, a queue of $n$ vehicles will form if $X_1\leq X_2$, and $X_1 \leq X_3$, and $\ldots$, and $X_1\leq X_n$, and $X_1>X_{n+1}$.
Since all variables are i.i.d., we can find the probability of all of these events to be true as the product of the individual probabilities:
\[p(N=n)=\begin{cases}
1 & n \leq 1 \\
\left[\prod_{i=2}^n p(X_i\geq X_1)\right]
p(X_{n+1}<X_1)
& n \geq 2
\end{cases}\]
Some thought before going on with the math should convince you that the final result does not depend on the distributions of the velocities.
Different distributions would affect how quickly queues form, but not their length after an infinite amount of time.
Indeed, since $X_1$ and $X_i$ are i.i.d., the probability that $X_1\leq X_i$ must be $1/2$.
Actually, for this we do not even need independence, but only exchangeability (which is implied by independence, and therefore holds in our case).
In our case, exchangeable random variables have the property that $p(X_1=x,X_i=x’)=p(X_1=x’,X_i=x)$.
This kind of symmetry means that there is no “preferred” ordering of the two velocities, and therefore the probability that one is larger than the other can only be $1/2$ (you can verify this formally by explicitly writing down and solving an integral for that probability).
Since $p(X_1\leq X_i)=1/2$, expanding the equation above gives:
\[p(N=n)=
p(X_{n+1}<X_1)\prod_{i=2}^n p(X_i\geq X_1)
=
\frac{1}{2} \prod_{i=2}^n \frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2^{n-1}}\]
Which holds again for $n>1$; For example, there is a probability of $1/2$ that there are at least two cars.
Finally, the expected value of $N$ is computed as
\[\mathbb{E}[N]=\sum_{n=1}^N n\cdot p(N=n)=\sum_{n=1}^N \frac{n}{2^n}=2\]
Therefore, the average number of cars in a queue is 2! Which definitely does not match my experience ;)
To conclude this (wrong, as we are going to see in a minute) solution, note that the derivation above was somewhat pedantic and brute-forced.
With a little bit more insight, one could realize that, assuming the velocities to be i.i.d., the number of vehicles in a queue is a random variable with Geometric distribution.
Each Bernoulli trial corresponds to a new vehicle entering the road and checking whether it is not faster than the queue of cars in front of it.
A Geometric random variable with parameter $p=1/2$ has the same distribution and expectation that we derived above.
Simulation
As I hinted at the beginning, the reasoning above is actually wrong, and I only realized that because I implemented a simulation and found completely different results.

data.title: Herbie detects inaccurate expressions and finds more accurate replacements
data.author: bwidlar
data.article_summary: Herbie是一款自动提升浮点运算精度的工具，能够检测不准确的表达式并找到更精确的替代方案。例如，将不准确的$\sqrt{x+1} - \sqrt{x}$替换为更准确的$\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+1} + \sqrt{x}}$。Herbie通过网页演示、教程和文档帮助用户了解和使用其功能。它还定期发布更新，如Herbie 2.2引入了新的平台API，Herbie 2.0优化了速度和精度等。Herbie项目还涉及与其他工具的整合和学术研究，如FPBench和Herbgrind。此外，Herbie团队积极参与各类学术会议和讲座，推广该工具并分享研究成果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Herbie工具的现状及其潜在发展方向，包括其在编译器中的集成以及在具体应用场景中的使用。

不同观点：
• tialaramex认为Herbie目前的功能很优秀，但更重要的洞见是将这种工具集成到编译器中的可能性。他设想未来的编程语言可以直接让开发者指定表达式的近似值，并给出精度和性能参数，类似于正则表达式的处理方式。
• RossBencina对tialaramex的观点表示感兴趣，但提到之前多次讨论中有人指出该工具在某些情况下表现不佳，并询问Herbie最近的更新情况。
• russfink提出了一个具体的技术问题，询问为什么表达式sqrt(x+1) - sqrt(x)对于所有x>1是不准确的，以及为什么1/(…)更好。
• TheFuzzball幽默地表示希望Herbie不要再出现问题（可能指之前的bug或不稳定表现）。
• ashirviskas好奇这种工具是否能帮助优化AI推理和训练引擎，或者这些引擎是否已经被优化到极致，并提到llama.cpp可能是一个很好的应用目标。
• 4gotunameagain称赞Herbie工具很棒，并分享了自己在使用Herbie进行长时间模拟以减少累积误差的经验。
• permalaise表示对Herbie的工作感到印象深刻，认为其具有价值。

补充讨论：
• 关于Herbie在编译器中的潜在集成以及其未来发展方向的讨论是一个重要议题，涉及到编程语言设计和浮点运算处理的简化。
• 对Herbie的具体技术问题（如russfink的问题）表明社区对工具的细节和数学原理仍有疑问。
• 一些评论（如TheFuzzball和RossBencina）提到了Herbie的稳定性和更新情况，显示出对工具可靠性和持续发展的关注。
• 应用场景的讨论（如ashirviskas和4gotunameagain的评论）展示了Herbie在实际问题（如AI优化和模拟）中的潜在价值。

data.title: Debounce
data.author: aanthonymax
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了编程中的去抖动（Debouncing）概念。去抖动通过在特定时间间隔内合并频繁触发的操作来避免过多执行，常用于处理用户输入，如在用户暂停输入后才执行搜索或过滤操作，以防止界面卡顿。去抖动与节流（Throttling）类似，但节流是限制连续操作的频率，而去抖动则是在操作暂停一段时间后才执行。去抖动分为"前缘"（leading edge）和"后缘"（trailing edge），通常在"后缘"执行函数，但具体实现可根据需求在"前缘"、"后缘"或两者上执行。去抖动确保操作至少间隔指定时间（如10毫秒）执行一次。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： debouncing的概念及其在不同场景下的应用和实现

不同观点：
• **[kazinator]**: 认为将去抖动（debouncing）与减少用户界面中的频繁搜索操作相类比是不恰当的。去抖动是为了解决开关信号的物理问题，而界面操作中，如果有足够的处理能力，每次按键都进行完整搜索是没有问题的，去抖动并不是必须的。开关去抖动与界面去抖动的应用场景不同，处理器速度越快，看到的抖动越多，去抖动问题不会因为更快的微控制器而消失。
  
• **[achou]**: 提到在使用去抖动或节流（throttle）处理异步函数时可能会引发意外行为，尤其是返回的结果可能是之前调用的Promise，而不是当前调用的结果。标准的lodash式实现不支持这种情况，需要特别注意实现是否符合预期。

• **[thomascountz]**: 分享了一个关于使用timeout和AbortController进行fetch去抖动的实现，并提供了示例链接。

• **[ncann]**: 提出在Java中实现去抖动的困难，标准库和常用工具库中缺乏合适的实现，并询问是否有好的推荐。

• **[lma21]**: 提到“合并”（Coalescing）这个术语，并提供了相关的维基百科链接，认为在某些情况下使用这个术语更合适。

• **[Pwntastic]**: 质疑该讨论的价值，认为这个话题并没有特别之处，不值得获得大量投票和关注。

• **[_def]**: 认为去抖动和界面操作的类比是合适的，具体取决于预期的行为，并提供了一个关于去抖动的资源链接。

• **[fnord77]**: 提供了关于开关抖动的维基百科链接。

• **[game_the0ry]**: 提到去抖动已成为前端面试中的热门问题。

• **[G_o_D]**: 通过类比解释了去抖动和节流的概念，并详细描述了它们在用户界面和网络请求处理中的应用场景。

• 去抖动在不同场景下的实现差异：如[ncann]提到的Java中缺乏合适的去抖动实现，[thomascountz]分享了具体的去抖动实现示例。
• 去抖动与节流的区别和应用：[G_o_D]详细解释了去抖动和节流在处理激进行为和网络请求中的不同作用和实现方式。

• 去抖动与界面操作的类比是否恰当，以及在不同场景下的具体实现和应用。

44787738.article_content:
Debouncing
, in the context of programming, means to discard operations that occur too close together during a specific interval, and consolidate them into a single invocation.
Debouncing is very similar to
throttling
. The key difference is that throttling enforces limits on continuous operations, while debouncing waits for invocations to stop for a specific time to consolidate many noisy invocations into one single invocation.
A typical use case of debouncing is when responding to user input. When the user is typing, no other action should be taken to avoid the UI becoming laggy. When the user pauses typing, we can start processing the input, such as filtering results, giving suggestions, etc. If the function
search
is debounced by 10 milliseconds, it means:
The first call to
search
is known as the
leading edge
.
For every next call to
search
, if it is within 10 milliseconds from the previous call, it is in the same "batch" as the previous call.
After 10 milliseconds have elapsed from the last call to
search
, if no other calls have happened, we have reached the
trailing edge
.
Usually,
search
is executed once on the trailing edge only, although sometimes it might be executed on the leading edge, or even both edges, depending on the specific use case. If executed on both edges, the debouncing implementation usually also ensures that the next leading edge invocation doesn't fire at least 10 milliseconds after the previous trailing edge.
See also
Glossary terms:
Throttle
Rate limit

on CSS-Tricks (April 6, 2016)

data.author: i_dont_know_

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI伦理与安全的实际应用、治理结构、以及伦理标准的争议

不同观点：
• **nisten**：认为AI伦理和安全组织的问题在于，他们的工作重点不是解决实际问题，如提高食品和住房的可负担性，而是放在缺乏“治理结构”上。他们往往不从事实际的技术工作，也不提出具体的解决方案，只是空谈伦理和安全问题。

• **Isamu**：指出AI伦理讨论中存在回避具体风险（如对人类的伤害）的倾向，而不是提供合理的论证来说明为什么某些概念（如阿西莫夫定律）过时。

• **i_dont_know_**：认为“AI伦理”被重新定义为关注虚构问题而不是现实世界的问题，并对此表示担忧。

• **lr4444lr**：将AI伦理比作核伦理，认为如果没有强有力的国际协议和后果，打破伦理的诱惑是巨大的。

• **mitthrowaway2**：认为伦理是一个广泛的领域，而安全只是其中的一个子集，许多伦理问题并不涉及安全问题。

• **mystraline**：质疑“伦理”的具体定义和公理，担心伦理被用作掩盖偏见和逃避质疑的工具。

• **parpfish**：更关注当前机器学习模型带来的伦理问题，如深度伪造和算法偏见，而不是未来可能出现的超级智能问题。

• **blibble**：认为当前一些科技领袖（如扎克伯格、马斯克等）已经是“不受约束的实体”，AI只会增加他们施加影响的范围和能力。

• **kyoob**：指出讨论从实际的治理和责任问题突然转向科幻场景（如AI接管世界），缺乏一贯性。

• **Workaccount2**：猜测可能越少的 safeguards 和 thought policing，模型的能力和泛化能力越强，从而使那些低 safeguards 的模型最强大。

• **saurik**：批评当前AI伦理工作更多关注公关问题，而不是实际的技术风险，如模型失控或接管世界，并认为模型的首要目标应该是完全服从用户指令。

• **akakajzbzbbx**：认为人类自身无法就什么是伦理/安全达成一致，因此对将伦理应用到AI上表示怀疑。

• **nathias**：质疑那些自称“伦理学家”的人的专业资质，认为许多所谓的伦理领域实际上只是公关部门。

• **p3rls**：以幽默的方式指出AI伦理讨论中的实际技术问题，如他们的机器人导致服务器过载。

data.title: Show HN: Stasher – Burn-after-read secrets from the CLI, no server, no trust
data.author: stasher-dev
data.article_summary: Stasher CLI是一款开源的命令行工具，用于安全、临时地分享秘密信息。它采用零知识加密（AES-256-GCM）在本地加密，并通过"阅后即焚"机制确保秘密只能被读取一次。Stasher没有后端服务器，不需注册账户，所有操作在终端完成，且10分钟后自动失效。所有代码和依赖都是公开且可验证的，确保透明性和安全性。用户可以通过`npx enstash`创建秘密并获取一个`uuid:key`，通过`npx destash`读取并永久删除该秘密。该工具适用于快速、安全地分享一次性密码、文件等敏感信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于密码分享工具的安全性、实现方式及信任问题

不同观点：
• [支持使用专用工具的观点]  
   有用户（如[indigodaddy]）推荐使用现有的密码分享工具如Password Pusher，认为其部署简单且功能合理，默认设置安全，是适合用于密码分享的工具。

• [质疑工具安全性的观点]  
   多位用户（如[Disposal8433]、[cmeacham98]、[pxc]）对该密码分享工具的安全性提出质疑。他们指出，工具的代码疑似由AI生成，项目作者匿名，且项目缺乏社区支持。这些因素使得用户不愿意信任该工具，尤其在安全敏感的场景下。

• [建议使用其他替代方案的观点]  
   有用户（如[i_proteus]、[precompute]）建议使用GPG等成熟的加密工具，或者对于非技术用户，推荐使用Signal、消失消息等更简便的方案。这些替代方案被认为更可靠且易于理解。

• [关于工具设计和流程的争议]  
   用户[coldstartops]质疑工具的流程设计，认为其将简单的两步操作复杂化，并引入服务器作为中间人，增加了风险。相比之下，[scosman]认为直接发送加密文本（如uuid:cipertext）也能达到相同的安全效果，且避免服务器接触敏感数据。

补充讨论：
• [服务器作用的疑问]  
   用户[h43z]询问服务器是否仅用于确保密码只被读取一次，表明对工具具体功能存在疑问。

• [“burn-after-read”概念的解释]  
   用户[oats]询问“burn-after-read”的含义，其他用户解释为密码在第一次读取后即不可再次获取。

• [命令行历史记录的安全问题]  
   用户[jijji]提到命令行操作可能被记录到.bash_history中，建议在执行敏感操作时调整历史记录设置以增强安全性。

• [盲目信任的争议]  
   用户[Thatdudeyouknow]简单表示“Trust me bro!”，这种盲目信任的态度与其他用户对安全性严格审查的态度形成对比，反映出在安全问题上不应轻率。

争议的焦点：工具的安全性、代码透明度、服务器的作用以及是否需要信任工具作者。

🛡️ Stasher CLI
Share secrets from your terminal. One-time only. No accounts. No backend. No BS.
🤔 Why?
I just wanted to share a password.
Not spin up a server. Not sign up for a "secure" web app.
Not trust a Slack thread. Just. Send. A. Secret.
So I built Stasher — a burn-after-read, command-line tool for secure, ephemeral secret sharing.
Built for people who are busy, paranoid, or both.
🔍 "How Can I Trust You?"
That's what someone asked me — and they were right to.
Even if I say:
"It's encrypted"
"The key never touches the server"
"No logs, no tracking, no metadata"...
How do you know I'm not lying?
🧠 I realized: the more secrecy your secrets require, the more transparency my system must offer.
So I built Stasher to prove itself.
🔐 Everything Is Verifiable
Every Stasher release:
✅ Is cryptographically signed with Cosign
✅ Includes a SLSA v1 provenance attestation
✅ Publishes a signed SBOM with all dependencies + licenses
✅ Is logged in the Rekor transparency log
✅ Comes with full verification instructions
📖 Every Line of Code Is Public
Everything that runs Stasher is open and verifiable:
🔧
CLI
🛰️
API
🖥️
App
⚙️
CI/CD
🌐
Website
🛡️ The only thing we don't expose? Your secret. Everything else is yours to inspect.
💡 Why You Might Actually Care
🔐
Zero-knowledge encryption
– AES-256-GCM, done locally
💣
Burn-after-read
– one use, then it's gone forever
🧰
CLI-first
– pipe it, script it, automate it
⚡
No setup
– just run it with
npx
⌛
10-minute expiry
– with proactive + reactive cleanup
📜
Full supply chain transparency
– signed, attested, and public
🚀 Try It Now
npx enstash
"
the launch code is 🍌-42
"
#
→ Outputs: uuid:key
npx destash
"
uuid:key
"
#
→ Reveals the secret and deletes it forever
🔐 Trust, But Actually Verify
#
Verify latest release
VERSION=
$(
npm view stasher-cli version
)
npm pack stasher-cli@
$VERSION
cosign verify-blob \
--certificate-identity-regexp=
"
https://github.com/stasher-dev/stasher-cli/.*
"
\
--certificate-oidc-issuer=https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
--signature=
"
stasher-cli-
$VERSION
.tgz.sig
"
\
"
stasher-cli-
$VERSION
.tgz
"
📚 More:
📖 Verification Overview
🔐 Cosign Signatures
🧾 SLSA Attestation
📋 SBOM Verification
📜 Rekor Transparency
🛠 Usage
Enstash (Create a Secret)
#
From a string
enstash
"
don't forget to feed the AI
"
#
From a file
cat .env
|
enstash
#
From stdin with npx
echo
"
my passphrase is secret123
"
|
npx enstash
Destash (Read + Burn)
destash
"
uuid:base64key
"
npx destash
"
uuid:base64key
"
Unstash (Manual Delete)
unstash
"
uuid
"
unstash
"
uuid:base64key
"
🧪 Examples
#
Share Wi-Fi password with a guest
npx enstash
"
yesits1234dontjudge
"
#
Send a one-time OTP via Slack
npx enstash
"
OTP: 842991
"
#
Share a deployment key, then delete it
echo
"
DEPLOY_KEY=super-secret
"
|
npx enstash
npx unstash
"
uuid
"
#
Send a secret via pigeon 🐦
npx enstash
"
vault code: 1234#
"
#
(Remind them: 10-minute expiry)
🔍 How It Works
🔐
Client-Side Encryption
Stasher encrypts with
AES-256-GCM
before sending anything
It uploads: ciphertext, IV, and tag —
never the key
You get a
uuid:base64key
token to share
⏱
Hybrid Expiry System
Reactive expiry
: validated on every access
Proactive cleanup
: background Durable Object alarms
Atomic
: each stash is guarded by its own isolated gatekeeper (one DO per UUID)
💥
Burn-After-Read
Once
destash
is called, the secret is revealed and the stash is burned
No replays, no race conditions —
guaranteed

npm install -g stasher-cli
…but honestly?

is faster and cleaner.

data.title: School AI surveillance can lead to false alarms, arrests
data.author: djoldman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[学校监控和政府干预的合理性及其对学生的影响]

不同观点：
• **反对过度监控和干预**  
  - [paradox460]和[malwrar]认为监控会让学生习惯于被监视，进而接受未来的大规模监控社会，这种“懒惰的压迫”对社会有害。  
  - [kayodelycaon]和[IshKebab]批评对13岁女孩的过度反应（如脱衣搜查和监禁），认为这种处理方式可能加剧问题而非解决。  
  - [Atreiden]指出，孩子因缺乏语境而说蠢话是正常的，自动联系执法部门是“反乌托邦”行为。  

• **支持监控但反对政府滥用**  
  - [tyleo]区分学校监控自有平台（可以接受）和政府监控私人通讯（不可接受），认为文章混淆了二者。  
  - [zahlman]指出学校因法律强制（如田纳西州零容忍政策）不得不采取极端措施，责任应归咎于政府而非企业。  

• **质疑监控的实际效果**  
  - [clwncr]质疑学校声称监控“阻止暴力”的说法，认为缺乏数据支持，且虚假 positives 的代价过高（如逮捕、心理评估）。  
  - [giantg2]批评执行者的懒惰，认为自动化系统的判断被盲目采信，导致过度反应。  

• **其他争议点**  
  - [SeanDav]提到法院的后续处理（如居家监禁）可能验证了事件的严重性，但缺乏家长通知仍不合理。  
  - [evaXhill]讽刺通过监控解决校园枪击的荒诞性，建议限制枪支获取而非侵犯隐私。  

补充讨论：  
- 争议焦点：监控的边界（如学校自有平台 vs. 私人通讯）、政府与学校的责任划分、虚假 positives 的社会代价。  
- 隐含讨论：如何平衡安全与自由，以及监控是否真正有效（如[ludicrousdispla]的讽刺暗示系统可能过度敏感）。

data.article_summary: Leonardo Chiariglione，一位拥有跨文化技术背景和基督教天主教教育背景的工程师，致力于开发可互操作的数字媒体技术。1987年，他创立了**MPEG（动态图像专家组）**，该组织在随后几年制定了多项重要标准，如MPEG-1、MPEG-2和MPEG-4，推动了数字媒体时代的到来。然而，由于一些不明势力的干预，MPEG逐渐失去活力，技术发展停滞，知识产权授权模式过时，导致行业和消费者无法受益于新技术。2020年6月，Chiariglione离开MPEG，随后于2020年7月提出成立**MPAI（人工智能编码的动态图像、音频和数据）**，旨在开发基于强大技术的新标准，打破僵局。MPAI已经制定了五项标准，并有多个项目正在进行中，涵盖AI应用、音频增强、多模态对话等领域。Chiariglione通过其著作和博客记录了MPEG的兴衰及MPAI的成长。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MPEG标准的兴衰、专利对技术发展的阻碍、以及新组织和技术的潜力

不同观点：
• **ZeroGravitas的观点**：认为MPEG引擎在技术和商业上已经失去动力，被大公司利用以谋取专利利益，阻碍了技术发展。这些公司通过专利设置障碍，限制了新技术的市场采用，导致行业受限，消费者无法受益。举例提到2002年Steve Jobs拒绝发布新版Quicktime，直到AAC许可问题得到解决。

• **wheybags的观点**：认为MPEG长期以来通过h264、h265和mp3等专利阻碍了行业发展。如果这些专利的铁腕控制被打破，可能会带来更多创新机会。

• **marcodiego的观点**：批评MPEG负责人过去的作为，认为其参与了专利垄断，并在失去权力后才抱怨。这种虚伪行为被视为“最精致的伪善”。

• **dostick的观点**：质疑所谓“ obscure forces”到底是什么，并提出疑问：作为一个开放标准的非营利组织，为何会受到阻碍？推测可能是因为技术上更优越的封闭标准出现，导致非营利项目难以竞争。提到USB联盟的成功例子，建议压缩标准可以类似方式发展。

• **kouru225的观点**：关注MPEG创始人新成立的组织MPAI，希望了解更多关于该组织的评价和技术细节。

• **mananaysiempre的观点**：提供背景信息，指出MPEG关闭时其所有页面和资料被删除并重定向至AI内容，暗示可能存在利益冲突。

• **karel-3d的观点**：对AI与视频编解码器的关系感到困惑，表明对两者的技术理解不深。

• **selvan的观点**：认为基于深度学习的专利免费视频编解码技术可能在几年内出现，提到微软开发的DCVC-RT编解码器，并讨论了AI在音视频编解码器开发中的潜力。

• **_bent的观点**：质疑MPAI社区提出的标准，认为某些标准没有必要，因为不同游戏服务器之间不需要互操作性。

• **zazazx的观点**：简短评论，强调行业对MPEG的利用和操纵。

• **gcr的观点**：欢迎MPEG组的结束，认为开放编解码器的兴起是积极的进展。虽然承认MPEG早期的工作有价值，但认为到2005年左右应转向更开放的互操作性模型。

• **scotty79的观点**：建议对知识产权持有者征收“财产税”以改善系统健康，批评版权制度阻碍创新，认为AI行业可能会摧毁这一制度。

补充讨论：
• **专利与技术发展**：多个评论提到了专利制度对技术发展的阻碍，尤其是MPEG相关的专利许可模型对行业和消费者的负面影响。
• **AI与编解码器的结合**：讨论了AI技术在未来编解码器开发中的潜在应用和优势，以及可能带来的创新。
• **非营利组织与商业标准的竞争**：探讨了非营利标准组织如何在面对商业技术竞争时保持竞争力，以及可能的组织模式借鉴。

争议焦点：
• **MPEG的功过**：一方认为MPEG早期贡献大，但后期阻碍了技术发展；另一方则认为其整体上是一个被大公司操控的专利垄断工具。
• **专利制度的存废**：讨论中涉及是否应通过征税或彻底打破专利制度来促进技术进步。

44822637.article_content:
Leonardo - one time video coding researcher, standardisation veteran and entrepreneur
I received a high-school education that gave me a Western classic imprint (Salesian Lyceum Valsalice, Maturità), an engineer’s  technical education (Polytechnic of Turin, MSc in Electronic Engineering) and a cross-cultural/technical experience (University of Tokyo, PhD in Electrical Communications).
My Christian Catholic education made and still makes me think that everybody should have a mission that extends beyond their personal interests.
In my early professional years, when digital media technologies were still maturing, I saw my mission in
the development of interoperable digital media technologies for
society
to enjoy
and
industry
to exploit
.
I needed an organisation that would
create digital media standards for
consumers
to seamlessly communicate and
industry
operate in a global market of interoperable products, services and applications
.
I conceived
t
hat organisation
in 1987, established it in 1988
I, and called
Moving Picture Experts Group
(MPEG). In four years,
MPEG had
ushered in the
digital media age
with
MPEG-1,
a standard for interactive media
used in Video CD, digital audio broadcasting (MP2), and personal music (MP3). Starting from the mid ’90s, MPEG-2, the result of the second MPEG project, became the common infrastructure that underpinned distribution of digital television via cable, satellite, terrestrial networks and package media (DVD). MPEG-4, the third standard first released in 1988, opened the way to digital media distribution over the internet. Several families of standards followed: MPEG-7, MPEG-21,
MPEG-A, MPEG-H, MPEG-I and more.
I chaired the group
fostering its productivity with the development of over 200 standards, membership with a 20-fold growth in attendance
from the initial 29 experts attending the first meeting, and scope extending from media to genomics, the “born digital” data of the world..
I closed MPEG on 2 June 2020 when I left because
obscure forces
had hijacked it.
Even before it has ceased to exists, the MPEG engine had run out of steam – technology- and business wise. The same obscure forces that have hijacked MPEG had kept it hostage to their interests impeding its technical development and keeping it locked to outmoded Intellectual Property licensing models delaying market adoption of MPEG standards. Industry has been strangled
and consumers have been deprived of the benefits of new technologies. From
facilitators
of new opportunities and experiences, MPEG s
tandards have morphed from
into
roadblocks.
On the 19th of July 2020 I proposed and, on 30 September 2020, a group of 33 companies established the
Moving Picture, Audio and Data Coding by Artificial Intelligence
(MPAI). Industry and consumers have now an organisation developing standards based on powerful technologies, overcoming stagnation and licensing stalemates. Five standards covering
execution of AI applications
,
audio enhancement
,
multimodal conversation
,
company performance prediction
, and
ecosystem governance
have been developed and adopted. More standards are in the pipeline:
AI-based End-to-End Video Coding
,
AI-Enhanced Video Coding
,
AI Health
,
Avatar Representation and Animation
,
Connected Autonomous Vehicles
,
Metaverse Model
,
Server-based Predictive Multiplayer Gaming
, and
XR Venues
.
The book
Even the stars die
tell the MPEG story from birth to death and the MPAI story from birth to growth to death. The book
Towards Pervasive and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
tells the MPAI story in its first 15 months of life: 5 standards produced and 7 projects under way1998.

data.title: Gemini CLI GitHub Actions
data.author: michael-sumner
data.article_summary: Gemini CLI GitHub Actions是一款免费、强大的AI编码辅助工具，适用于团队协作。它可以作为自主代理自动处理常规编码任务，也可以作为按需协作伙伴，接受任务委派。该工具通过触发事件（如新问题或拉取请求）在后台异步工作，利用项目全 context 自动处理任务，如智能问题分类、加速拉取请求审查和按需协作等。它具备企业级安全和控制，支持无凭证认证、细粒度控制和完全透明。现已推出beta版，全球可用，存储库位于google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli。用户可自定义工作流并贡献代码，免费配额丰富，支持Google AI Studio及Vertex AI等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Gemini产品及其相关工具（CLI、GitHub Action、API等）的用户体验和功能争议

不同观点：
• **对产品定位和命名混乱的批评**：
  - [thecupisblue] 认为Google在产品定位上缺乏清晰的战略，导致多个相似产品（如Gemini、Jules等）出现自我竞争，用户感到困惑。
  - [artdigital] 和 [gundmc] 同样对"Gemini CLI"的名称表示质疑，认为其主要通过GitHub使用，称为"GitHub Action"更为合适。

• **对功能和用户体验的不满**：
  - [thecupisblue] 指出Gemini的文档分散，API SDK不统一，功能受限且使用繁琐，对普通用户不友好。
  - [grogenaut] 强调Gemini在日历预约、Google文档编辑等基本功能上的不足，认为Google未能在其生态系统中充分利用AI。
  - [PanMan] 认为设置过程复杂，需要Google Cloud项目，不如GitHub的Cursor Bot简便。

• **对产品潜力的认可与期望**：
  - [jtrn] 试图厘清Gemini工具的本质，认为其在GitHub Actions环境中的应用具有潜力，但需要简化理解过程。
  - [turblety] 希望Google能提供更简单的订阅模式，方便开发者使用多种Gemini工具。

• **与其他工具的比较**：
  - [ssalka] 认为Claude Code比Gemini更有效且便宜。
  - [ncrmro] 则表示Copilot Agent在某些场景下表现出色，Gemini需要更具优势才能替代现有工具。

• **对隐私和安全的关注**：
  - [brtkwr] 对Gemini的免费提供表示怀疑，担心隐私问题，尤其在私有/内部仓库中使用时需谨慎。

补充讨论：
• **对特定功能的兴趣**：
  - [elpakal] 仅对PR审查功能感兴趣，显示出用户对具体功能的需求差异。
  
• **对产品改进的建议和实验**：
  - [stillsut] 分享了其在优化开源代码库审查流程上的实验和框架，以应对AI生成PR的质量问题。

争议焦点：
• Google Gemini产品线的定位不清晰、功能分散、用户体验差以及与竞争产品的比较。

Meet your new AI coding teammate: Gemini CLI GitHub Actions
Aug 06, 2025
·
Share
Twitter
Facebook
LinkedIn
Mail
Copy link
Gemini CLI GitHub Actions is a no-cost, powerful AI coding teammate for your repository. It acts both as an autonomous agent for critical routine coding tasks, and an on-demand collaborator you can quickly delegate work to.
Jerop Kipruto
Senior Software Engineer
Ryan J. Salva
Senior Director, Product Management
Share
Twitter
Facebook
LinkedIn
Mail
Copy link
In June, we launched
Gemini CLI
, an open-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini to your terminal. The enthusiastic adoption from developers has been incredible. To keep up with the flood of feature requests and contributions, we put our own tool to the test — using Gemini CLI to automate issue triage and pull request reviews. When community members noticed our new workflows, they asked us to share what we’ve built.
Today, we’re introducing
Gemini CLI GitHub Actions
. It’s a no-cost, powerful AI coding teammate for your repository. It acts both as an autonomous agent for critical routine coding tasks, and an on-demand collaborator you can quickly delegate work to.
It’s now in beta, available to everyone worldwide, and you can find it on GitHub at
google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli
.
An AI teammate in your repository
While Gemini CLI is a tool built for individual use in your own terminal, Gemini CLI GitHub Actions was created for team collaboration on the platform where developers work with each other.
Triggered by events like new issues or pull requests, it works asynchronously in the background, using the full context of your project to automatically handle tasks. It knows your code, understands what you want to do, and gets it done.
We’re launching with three powerful, open-source workflows that can help you code better, faster:
🤖Intelligent issue triage
: Automate the overhead of managing new issues. Gemini CLI can analyze, label and prioritize incoming issues, helping focus your attention on what matters most.
🚀Accelerated pull request reviews
: Get instant, insightful feedback on code changes. Gemini CLI can review pull requests for quality, style and correctness, freeing up reviewers to focus on more complex tasks and decisions.
🤝On-demand collaboration
: Simply mention @gemini-cli in any issue or pull request to delegate tasks. Tell it to do things like, "write tests for this bug," "implement the changes suggested above," "brainstorm alternative solutions," or "fix this well defined bug."
Easily create new feature requests on GitHub for Gemini CLI to handle on your behalf
Gemini CLI GitHub Actions can handle your pull requests, providing code changes and AI-generated suggestions for improving the user experience
Delegate work with an "@gemini-cli" tag and the agent can complete a range of tasks, from writing bugs to fixing bugs
Think of these initial workflows as your launchpad. They are open-source and fully customizable — you can create your own workflows, or configure the ones that come built into Gemini CLI GitHub Actions.
Built with enterprise-grade security and control
Robust security measures are a fundamental part of modern software development. That’s why we built Gemini CLI GitHub Actions with security and flexibility at its core.
You are always in control with capabilities including:
Secure, credential-less authentication:
Vertex AI and Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise users can tap into Google Cloud's
Workload Identity Federation
(WIF) to eliminate the need for long-lived API keys in your environment, drastically reducing the risk of credential compromise.
Granular control
: Enforce the principle of least privilege with multi-layered controls. Use capabilities like command allowlisting to explicitly approve every shell command the agent can execute. You can also create a custom identity for the agent (e.g., gemini-for-your-org) and grant it only the precise permissions it needs.
Complete transparency:
GitHub on CLI comes integrated with
OpenTelemetry
, an industry standard for telemetry, so you can stream logs and metrics to your preferred observability platform, like Google Cloud Monitoring. This gives you full, real-time visibility into every action to monitor usage and debug complex workflows.
Get started today
What will you build with your new coding teammate? A workflow that automatically generates release notes? One that keeps documentation in sync with your code? Don’t just imagine it; build it. We invite you to contribute your innovative workflows to our repository and share them with the community.
Gemini CLI GitHub Actions is
available today
in beta, with
generous free-of-charge quotas
for Google AI Studio. Vertex AI, along with the Standard and Enterprise tiers of Gemini Code Assist, are also supported. We will have free-of-charge use for Gemini Code Assist for individual users available soon.

44783372.article_content:
Splatshop: Efficiently Editing Large Gaussian Splat Models
Markus Schütz, Christoph Peters, Florian Hahlbohm, Elmar Eisemann, Marcus Magnor, Michael Wimmer.
2025–06 in
Computer Graphics Forum (Proc. HPG)
44, 8.
Official version
Abstract
We present Splatshop, a highly optimized toolbox for interactive editing (selection, deletion, painting, transformation, ...) of 3D Gaussian Splatting models. Utilizing a comprehensive collection of heuristic approaches, we carefully balance between exact and fast rendering to enable precise editing without sacrificing real-time performance. Our experiments confirm that Splatshop achieves these goals for scenes with up to 100 million primitives. We also show how our proposed pipeline can be extended for use with head-mounted displays. As such, Splatshop is the first VR-capable editor for large-scale 3D Gaussian Splatting models and a step towards a “Photoshop for Gaussian Splatting.”
Images
Notes
This work has been presented at HPG 2025 on June 24th. The paper has been published on June 21st.

data.title: Show HN: Aura – Like robots.txt, but for AI actions
data.author: OsmanDKitay
data.article_summary: AURA（Agent-Usable Resource Assertion）是一个开放协议，旨在使网站变得机器可读，替代脆弱的屏幕抓取和DOM操作。它通过一个声明式的`aura.json` manifest文件，让网站以安全、高效和标准化的API形式向AI代理暴露其功能。核心概念包括Manifest文件（位于`/.well-known/aura.json`）定义网站能力，Capability描述具体操作（如`create_post`），以及动态HTTP头`AURA-State`提供上下文信息。该协议提供了NPM包和参考服务器实现，帮助网站实现AURA兼容，并展示了如何通过AI代理执行网站功能。这将改变AI与网站交互的方式，从猜测性操作转变为声明式交互。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[AURA文件标准的可行性和必要性]

不同观点：
• **支持AURA标准的观点**
  - 提出AURA可以替代脆弱的屏幕抓取和DOM操作，提供更健壮、安全和高效的机器可读层。
  - 类似于站点地图（sitemap），但更专注于AI与网络的交互。

• **反对AURA标准的观点**
  - 类似于robots.txt，AURA标准无法强制执行，存在恶意网站提供错误信息的风险（如故意提供误导性数据）。
  - 网站所有者可能不愿意采用此标准，例如Reddit移除API后，用户转向抓取网站本身。
  - 现有的OpenAPI或语义网标准已足够，AURA可能是重复发明轮子。

• **质疑AURA的实际用途**
  - 除非网站是付费的，否则没有动力采用AURA，因为广告收入依赖于人类用户。
  - AI代理的本意是能够自行理解和抓取内容，AURA可能违背了这一初衷。

补充讨论：
- **技术实现争议**：有人建议AURA应通过URL或内容协商（如`<script type="text/llm">`或HTTP头）实现，而非单独文件。
- **AI伦理争议**：部分评论者批评AURA是迎合少数公司（如LLM开发者）的需求，可能损害网络的开放性。
- **采用率问题**：语义网标签的采用率一直很低，AURA可能面临同样的问题。

AURA: The Protocol for a Machine-Readable Web
AURA (Agent-Usable Resource Assertion)
is an open protocol for making websites understandable and operable by AI agents. It proposes a new standard for AI-web interaction that moves beyond fragile screen scraping and DOM manipulation towards a robust, secure, and efficient machine-readable layer for the internet.
The web was built for human eyes. AURA is a specification for giving it a machine-readable "API".
The Vision: Why AURA?
Current AI agents interact with websites in a brittle and inefficient way:
Screen Scraping:
They "look" at pixels and guess where to click. This is slow, expensive, and breaks with the slightest UI change.
DOM Manipulation:
They parse complex HTML structures, which are inconsistent across sites and change frequently.
Insecurity:
Website owners have no control over what an agent might do.
AURA solves this by allowing websites to
declare their capabilities
in a simple, standardized
aura.json
manifest file.
Instead of an agent guessing how to "create a post," the website explicitly states:
"I have a capability named
create_post
. It's an
HTTP POST
to
/api/posts
and requires
title
and
content
parameters."
This is a fundamental paradigm shift from
imperative guessing
to
declarative interaction
.
Core Concepts
Manifest (
aura.json
):
A file served at
/.well-known/aura.json
that acts as a site's "API documentation" for AI agents. It defines all available resources and capabilities.
Capability:
A single, discrete action an agent can perform (e.g.,
list_posts
,
login
,
update_profile
). Each capability maps to a specific HTTP request.
State (
AURA-State
Header):
A dynamic HTTP header sent by the server with each response, informing the agent about the current context (e.g., is the user authenticated?) and which capabilities are currently available to them.
This Repository
This repository is the
canonical specification for the AURA protocol
. It provides the core building blocks for the AURA ecosystem:
packages/aura-protocol
: The core
@aura/protocol
NPM package, containing TypeScript interfaces and the official JSON Schema for validation.
This is the heart of AURA.
packages/reference-server
: A reference implementation of an AURA-enabled server built with Next.js. Use this to understand how to make your own website AURA-compliant.
packages/reference-client
: A minimal, backend-only reference client demonstrating two powerful ways to consume the protocol, without any browser or extension required.
Getting Started: A 5-Minute Demonstration
See the protocol in action.
1. Install Dependencies
From the root of the monorepo, install all necessary dependencies for all packages.
pnpm install
2. Run the Reference Server
The server is a sample website that "speaks" AURA.
#
This will start the server (usually on http://localhost:3000)
pnpm --filter aura-reference-server dev
You can now visit
http://localhost:3000/.well-known/aura.json
in your browser to see the manifest.
3. Run the Reference Agent
This simple agent uses an LLM to understand a prompt and execute a capability on the server.
First, create a
.env
file inside the
packages/reference-client
directory and add your OpenAI API key.
OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
Then, run the agent with a URL and a prompt:
#
(In a new terminal)
pnpm --filter aura-reference-client agent -- http://localhost:3000
"
list all the blog posts
"
Observe how the agent fetches the manifest, plans its action, and executes the list_posts capability directly.
4. Run the Crawler (The Big Vision)
This script demonstrates how a search engine could index an AURA-enabled site, understanding its functions, not just its content.
#
In the client directory
pnpm --filter aura-reference-client crawler -- http://localhost:3000
The output shows a structured JSON object representing the site's capabilities. This is the future of search: indexing acti

data.title: Children's movie leads art historian to long-lost Hungarian masterpiece (2014)
data.author: how-about-this
data.article_summary: 艺术史学家Gergely Barki在观看电影《精灵鼠小弟》时，意外发现匈牙利先锋派画家Róbert Berény的失踪已久的画作《Sleeping Lady with Black Vase》被用作道具。这幅画自1920年代消失后，一直下落不明。Barki通过多封电子邮件联系到电影制作方，得知画作被前任布景设计师从古董店购得，之后卖给私人收藏家。这幅画将于12月13日在布达佩斯拍卖，起拍价约为11万欧元。Berény曾是战前先锋艺术团体“八人组”的领袖，后因政治原因逃亡柏林，其作品因历史动荡而四散流失。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Berény的画作《Sleeping Lady with Black Vase》的历史背景、所有权变迁及其现状

不同观点：
• evaXhill认为这幅画具有重要的历史背景，对它最终流入私人收藏感到遗憾。他提到Berény在第一次世界大战后从柏林返回布达佩斯，而该画作曾在1928年于恩斯特博物馆展出，后来被卖出。evaXhill推测买家可能是犹太人，并在二战期间或之前离开了匈牙利。他强调该画作具有重要历史意义，且是Berény的优秀作品之一，对其现状表示惋惜。

• cafard没有直接讨论画作本身，而是对传闻中Berény与Anastasia的绯闻提出讽刺性评论，暗示某些读者可能会对此类八卦消息一笑而过，而不是深入了解画作本身的艺术和历史价值。这表明他对讨论名人私生活的倾向有所不满。

• j-kent则对画作的重现和即将被拍卖感到高兴，认为这是“人文领域的胜利”。他的观点与evaXhill形成鲜明对比，认为画作进入私人收藏并通过拍卖被重新发现是一个积极的事件，而没有关注其历史背景和可能的遗憾。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于对艺术品流入私人收藏的态度。evaXhill对此表示遗憾，认为具有历史意义的艺术品应该被公开展示，而j-kent则对此表示欢迎，认为拍卖是艺术品重见天日的机会。
• cafard的评论引入了一个与主讨论点无关的八卦话题，暗示对讨论名人私生活的倾向，这在一定程度上偏离了对画作本身的讨论。

Stuart Little leads art historian to long-lost Hungarian masterpiece
This article is more than 10 years old
Researcher spots Sleeping Lady with Black Vase by Robert Bereny being used as a prop in Hollywood children’s movie
Agence France-Presse in Budapest
Thu 27 Nov 2014 13.02 EST
Last modified on Wed 19 Oct 2022 10.29 EDT
Share
A long-lost avant garde painting has returned to
Hungary
after nine decades thanks to a sharp-eyed art historian, who spotted it being used as a prop in the Hollywood film Stuart Little.
Gergely Barki, 43, a researcher at Hungary’s national gallery in Budapest, noticed Sleeping Lady with Black Vase by Róbert Berény as he watched television with his daughter Lola in 2009.
“I couldn’t believe my eyes when I saw Bereny’s long-lost masterpiece on the wall behind Hugh Laurie. I nearly dropped Lola from my lap,” said Barki. “A researcher can never take his eyes off the job, even when watching Christmas movies at home.”
The painting disappeared in the 1920s, but Barki recognised it immediately even though he had only seen a faded black-and-white photo from an exhibition in 1928.
The big-eyed children: the extraordinary story of an epic art fraud
Read more
He sent a flurry of emails to staff at the film’s makers, Sony Pictures and Columbia Pictures, and received a reply from a former set designer on the film – two years later.
“She said the picture had been hanging on her wall,” Barki said.
“She had snapped it up for next to nothing in an antiques shop in Pasadena, California, thinking its avant garde elegance was perfect for Stuart Little’s living room.”
After leaving Sony, she sold the painting to a private collector who has now brought the picture to Budapest for sale by auction.
Berény, the leader of a pre-first world war avant garde movement called the Group of Eights, fled to Berlin in 1920 after designing recruitment posters for Hungary’s short-lived communist revolution in 1919.
In the German capital, he had a romance with the actor Marlene Dietrich, and – according to Barki – is also rumoured to have had a fling with Anastasia, the mysterious daughter of Russia’s last tsar, Nicholas II.
Berény’s painting will be sold on 13 December, with a starting price of around €110,000 (£87,000), staff at the Virag Judit auction house said.
According to Barki, the buyer at the 1928 exhibition, who was possibly Jewish, is likely to have left Hungary before or during the second world war.
“After the wars, revolutions and tumult of the 20th century, many Hungarian masterpieces are lost, scattered around the world,” he said.

• evaXhill认为这幅画具有重要的历史背景，对它最终流入私人收藏感到遗憾。他提到Berény在第一次世界大战后从柏林返回布达佩斯，而该画作曾在1928年于恩斯特博物馆展出，后来被卖出。evaXhill推测买家可能是犹太人，并在二战期间或之前离开了匈牙利。他强调该画作具有重要历史意义，且是Berény的优秀作品之一，对其现状表示惋惜。

• cafard没有直接讨论画作本身，而是对传闻中Berény与Anastasia的绯闻提出讽刺性评论，暗示某些读者可能会对此类八卦消息一笑而过，而不是深入了解画作本身的艺术和历史价值。这表明他对讨论名人私生活的倾向有所不满。

• j-kent则对画作的重现和即将被拍卖感到高兴，认为这是“人文领域的胜利”。他的观点与evaXhill形成鲜明对比，认为画作进入私人收藏并通过拍卖被重新发现是一个积极的事件，而没有关注其历史背景和可能的遗憾。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于对艺术品流入私人收藏的态度。evaXhill对此表示遗憾，认为具有历史意义的艺术品应该被公开展示，而j-kent则对此表示欢迎，认为拍卖是艺术品重见天日的机会。
• cafard的评论引入了一个与主讨论点无关的八卦话题，暗示对讨论名人私生活的倾向，这在一定程度上偏离了对画作本身的讨论。

data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了Craigslist创始人克雷格·纽马克（Craig Newmark）的慈善事业及其对新闻业的影响，重点分析了Craigslist如何在1995年创立后逐渐取代报纸的分类广告业务。纽马克认为，Craigslist对报纸业务的冲击被夸大了，真正的原因在于报纸失去了读者，电视等媒体的兴起也起到了重要作用。尽管Craigslist只是众多新兴数字平台之一，但它象征了报纸行业的巨大转变。文章还描述了纽马克的创业历程，他从一个计算机工程师转变为一个无意成为企业家的创业者，并讲述了Craigslist如何从一个为朋友提供信息的小列表发展为年收入数亿美元的平台。纽马克自认不善管理，聘请了Jim Buckmaster作为CEO，二人共同坚持不以最大化利润为目标的经营理念，拒绝了可能带来更大商业利益的扩展想法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Craigslist是否导致报纸业衰落，以及报纸业衰落的其他原因]

不同观点：
• **Craigslist是报纸衰落的主要原因之一**  
  - 报纸未能适应互联网技术，拒绝在高层引入技术人才（silvestrov）  
  - 报纸的分类广告收入原本支撑其运营，Craigslist抢占了这一市场（JKCalhoun）  
  - 小城市可以自建类似Craigslist的平台，无需依赖广告（initramfs）  
• **Craigslist并非唯一或主要原因**  
  - 传统新闻业面临多重压力，Craigslist只是其中之一（ghaff）  
  - 其他地区（如国家X）没有Craigslist但报纸业同样衰落（stevoski）  
  - 在线广告（如Google）才是报纸衰落的真正原因（thomasingalls）  
• **技术或商业模式的其他讨论**  
  - Craigslist的成功部分归功于Perl技术（cutler）  
  - 分类广告仍存在，但互联网普及受限（5pl1n73r）  
  - Craigslist拒绝扩张（如用户评论功能）是正确选择（rightbyte）  

补充讨论：  
- 报纸的商业模式本身可能已存在问题（JKCalhoun）  
- 小规模分类广告出版物（如The Want Advertiser）更受Craigslist冲击（MontgomeryPy）  
- 字体设计影响阅读体验（indigodaddy）  
- Betteridge法则（标题为疑问句时答案通常为“否”）及其他国家案例（bux93）

Analysis
Business & Work
Craigslist founder Craig Newmark sits in his home office in New York, on Thursday, Feb. 9, 2023. Newmark earned a spot on the Chronicle of Philanthropy's "Philanthropy 50" list that year for his donations to charitable causes focusing on cybersecurity and journalism. (AP Photo/Robert Bumsted)
By:
Rick Edmonds
July 31, 2025
This article is part of
The Poynter 50
, a series reflecting on 50 moments and people that shaped journalism over the past half-century — and continue to influence its future. As Poynter celebrates its 50th anniversary, we examine how the media landscape has evolved and what it means for the next era of news.
The decline of newspaper print classifieds and the ripple effects that gutted newsrooms began,
by many accounts
, in 1995. That’s when Craig Newmark invented Craigslist, the homely but oh-so-successful site that matches buyers and sellers, mostly for free, with only a few listings carrying a modest charge.
Did Craigslist drive the downfall of print classifieds?
“I’ve always wondered about that,” Newmark said in a Zoom interview July 1. “I think it had an effect.”
But portraying him and the list as torpedoing an otherwise great business model is way overblown, he still believes. Citing
an influential essay by Thomas Baekdal
, Newmark contends that the root of newspapers’ trouble was the loss of readers.
“TV hit hard. … (And) l’m like the folks on ‘CSI,’ I follow the evidence. That goes back at least to the ’60s.”
Bad in itself, the loss also took away newspapers’ dominant share of local audiences and ability to charge premium classified ad rates. The slide in circulation looks even worse, Baekdal pointed out, when compared to continued increases in the number of households over the years.
Still, Craigslist came to symbolize the shift. Dozens of other vertical digital sites cropped up, before and after, all offering a deadly competitive pairing of an effective and much cheaper service than newspaper classifieds. Even if Craigslist was just one of many, though, it was arguably Newmark who put a face on the massive disruption.
Here in six short chapters is the tale of Craigslist’s rise to a business generating hundreds of millions of dollars a year, how Newmark has used that fortune and how newspapers, slow to adapt, failed to respond effectively to the digital shift. It’s based on information already on record, supplemented by analysis and color from my interview with Newmark.
Chapter 1: The early years
When Newmark launched Craigslist, he was in his early 40s with two decades of experience as a computer engineer, including a long stint at IBM, later consulting at large firms like Charles Schwab.
He wasn’t a media mogul or startup evangelist. He was, by his own admission, a socially awkward nerd. (“Nerd” appears in the
one-sentence mission statement
for his foundation.) That sensibility shaped what would become Craigslist.
Craig Newmark in a cubicle in an undated photo. (Courtesy: Craig Newmark)
Newmark said he was more comfortable replying to user emails from a distance. For a decade and a half, he called himself a customer service representative, not CEO.
Craig’s definition of his role is revealing. He saw himself as a builder of a simple tool that created a community of users. Toppling the news industry business model was not the point at all.
Chapter 2: Accidental entrepreneur?
Craiglist’s beginnings are a twice-told story. At first, it was literally a list for Newmark’s circle of friends about interesting goings-on in the San Francisco Bay area. Soon, Newmark added swaps and free ads for things like furniture and refrigerators. Before long, he expanded to other big cities and began generating income by charging for job and real estate listings, turning the hobby into a business.
But Newmark didn’t want to run a company. “I’m a terrible manager,” he said. “I’m just not emotionally suited to making tough decisions.”
As growth took off over the first five years, he continued as owner but hired fellow programmer Jim Buckmaster and quickly promoted him to CEO — a position he still holds today.
Programming and Craigslist CEO Jim Buckmaster, left, and Craig Newmark in an undated photo. (Courtesy: Craig Newmark)
Buckmaster, an off-and-on graduate student for 10 years at the University of Michigan who occasionally contributed haikus to the Craigslist site, is as unconventional as Newmark. His official bio notes that
he has been called a democratic socialist and a communist
. He and Newmark are neither, he wrote, but rather the kind of capitalists who are not fully focused on maximizing profit.
That ethos defined the company. Newmark and Buckmaster rebuffed ideas for expansion — like adding user reviews — because it would make Craigslist easier to game and harder to moderate. (Review sites like Yelp and Airbnb have turned out to have exactly that challenge.)

主要讨论点：AI在软件开发和行业中的作用及影响

不同观点：
• **AI提高效率还是降低效率**：
  - **djoldman**：引用研究指出，AI可能使有经验的开发人员变慢，质疑广泛应用AI的效益。
  - **toddmorey**：认为AI在处理不喜欢的任务（如设计）上表现出色，暗示个人偏好影响对AI的看法。

• **AI和AGI的未来**：
  - **smokel**：认为即使首先创造出AGI的公司也不一定获得最大声誉，历史证明营销能力往往决定声誉归属。
  - **lowsong**：对AGI的不可避免性提出质疑，认为当前处于AI hype bubble中，且没有证据表明AGI即将到来。

• **AI工具的主要受益者**：
  - **netown**：认为AI工具的最大受益者不是开发人员，而是不写代码的周边人员，质疑行业内对AI作用的认知。

• **AI在管理和任务总结中的潜力**：
  - **dude250711**：认为AI在管理任务总结上表现出色，建议开发针对高管的"GPT Middle Manager"工具以削减管理成本。

• **对AI和开发人员角色的个人态度**：
  - **sp527**：批评某些开发人员出于自我保护而故意引入复杂性，并质疑他们对AI的复杂态度。
  - **demirbey05**：对AI取代重复任务的乐观态度表示不解，指出在资本主义社会中这种乐观可能不现实。

补充讨论：
- **研究方法的有效性**：djoldman对研究的小样本和广泛结论的有效性提出质疑。
- **AI在非开发领域的应用**：netown提到AI在开发领域外的应用较少，并引发对行业认知的讨论。
- **AI对工作和生活平衡的影响**：demirbey05质疑AI在资本主义社会中对工作生活平衡的实际影响。

data.title: Photographer spends years on street corner capturing same commuters daily (2017)
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 丹麦摄影师Peter Funch在9年时间里，每天早上在纽约42街和范德比尔特大道的街角拍摄通勤者。他的项目《42nd and Vanderbilt》捕捉到同一个人在通勤途中的瞬间，让观众思考这些照片是否相隔几天、几个月甚至几年。通过这种简单的监视式拍摄，Funch展示了人们日常的习惯和孤独感，揭示了早晨通勤的单调和个体的独特性。作家Douglas Copeland将这个角落形容为城市中常见的无名之地，如同空白画布，让人们在重复中看到不同的细节变化。Funch的作品邀请观众观察、分解每张照片，发现什么变了，什么保持不变，反映出我们日常生活中容易忽视的小仪式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一个展示相同个体在不同时期照片项目的不同看法与联想

不同观点：
• [cs702] 认为该项目很有趣，特别是个体在多年后依然保持一致的神态和风格，令人着迷。
• [PorterBHall] 分享了个人经历，提到在自己小社区中遇到曾经的通勤伙伴，虽然能认出他们，但明显感觉他们都变老了，同时反思自己可能也一样。
• [FrameworkFred] 引用了电影《Smoke》中的一句话，暗示随着时间推移，不同的人可能变得相似，而曾经相似的人可能消失，带有一种哲理性。
• [rapnie] 将项目与现代科技影响下的社会变化联系起来，提到Ritzo Ten Cate的“Caught in the App”项目，展示了人们被科技设备“控制”的状态，反映社会的快速变化。
• [fennecfoxy] 对街头摄影的隐私问题进行了讨论，指出人们在公共场合没有隐私权，同时分享了自己使用不同摄影设备的体验，强调了胶片摄影的独特魅力。
• [JR1427] 对项目中照片拍摄时间的间隔提出质疑，认为大多数照片对并没有相隔很长时间。
• [moi2388] 对项目的真实性提出质疑，认为照片中人物的衣着、发型和配饰过于一致，且没有显示出应有的年龄变化。

补充讨论：
• 该项目引发了对时间流逝和个体变化的反思，尤其是在外表和风格上的稳定性。
• 有人将项目与现代科技对社会的影响联系起来，扩展了讨论的范围。
• 对项目真实性的质疑引发了对照片内容可信度的讨论。
• 摄影设备和技术的选择也成为讨论的一部分，反映出不同摄影形式对拍摄体验的影响。

争议焦点：
• 项目中照片的真实性及其时间间隔的准确性受到质疑，部分观众对人物变化的一致性表示怀疑。

Photographer Spends 9 Years on One Street Corner Capturing Same Commuters Every Day
By
Jessica Stewart
on November 5, 2017
For 9 years, from 8:30 am and 9:30 am, Danish photographer
Peter Funch
stood at the southern corner of 42nd Street and Vanderbilt Avenue. In the rush of commuters, what he found was a glimpse of universal habits and the long trek to work. From 2007 to 2016 Funch carried out his project
42nd and Vanderbilt
in which he captures the same person twice, mid-commute, leaving the viewer to wonder if they were photographed days, months, or even years apart.
This simple surveillance exercise lets viewers ponder the small daily rituals we take for granted and also invited them into as an observer, picking apart each image to discover what has changed and what remains the same. In these stolen moments, we see Funch's subjects lost in thought, fraught with worry, even eyes closed as if in divine ecstasy. Within a sea of people, they tend to isolate themselves, holding on to the last bit of solitude before entering the workplace.
“The corner of 42nd Street and Vanderbilt Avenue…what’s that? It’s a patch of nowhere that hides, like similar patches of nowhere, in all cities everywhere,”
writes
acclaimed novelist and artist Douglas Copeland of the work. “It's the space of Edward Hopper. It's the real estate equivalent of a Styrofoam packing peanut. It's blank, and it's in this blankness that we circle back to Warhol and repetition and the aesthetic experience we enjoy when we look from one Marilyn to the next to see which screened face has what kind of silkscreen printing error.”
Shocking in its raw vision of the banality of our morning routine, it's both amusing—and telling—which details viewers immediately focus on. Whether it's wearing the same outfit or not donning a happy smile. Though Funch's subjects aren't “picture perfect,” they are real.
See more of Peter Funch's insightful street photography series in his new book
42nd and Vanderbilt
.
For
42nd and Vanderbilt
, photographer Peter Funch spent 9 years documenting the morning commute on a street corner in New York.
His work leaves us wondering if these people were captured days, minutes, weeks, or even years, apart.

44823123.article_summary: 丹麦摄影师Peter Funch在9年时间里，每天早上在纽约42街和范德比尔特大道的街角拍摄通勤者。他的项目《42nd and Vanderbilt》捕捉到同一个人在通勤途中的瞬间，让观众思考这些照片是否相隔几天、几个月甚至几年。通过这种简单的监视式拍摄，Funch展示了人们日常的习惯和孤独感，揭示了早晨通勤的单调和个体的独特性。作家Douglas Copeland将这个角落形容为城市中常见的无名之地，如同空白画布，让人们在重复中看到不同的细节变化。Funch的作品邀请观众观察、分解每张照片，发现什么变了，什么保持不变，反映出我们日常生活中容易忽视的小仪式。
