data.title: About the BLOBs in Ventoy
data.author: turrini
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Ventoy项目中关于二进制大对象（BLOBs）的问题。Ventoy是100%开源项目，但使用了一些来自其他开源项目的二进制文件。文章提出，为了提高透明度和管理这些BLOBs，可以创建GitHub子仓库，通过GitHub的CI构建一次这些二进制文件并在Ventoy中使用。如果发现问题，可以更新源代码并重新构建。文章还列出了当前Ventoy源码中所有的BLOBs文件，并提供了构建说明和来源链接。最后，作者询问了GitHub是否能为FreeBSD、Windows以及不同Linux环境提供构建环境，并邀请社区帮助完善BLOBs列表。

It should be noted firstly that Ventoy is 100% open souce and everything is transparent.

data.title: Cursed Knowledge
data.author: bqmjjx0kac
data.article_summary: 本文列出了一些在开发Immich项目过程中遇到的“诅咒”知识，即一些意外且令人困扰的技术问题。主要包括：Zitadel的自定义脚本不支持正则表达式的命名捕获组；Microsoft Entra不在其OpenID文档中包含PKCE支持，导致误解；EXIF元数据中的图像尺寸可能与实际不符；YAML的空格处理不直观；Windows隐藏文件无法用"w"标志打开；Bash脚本中的回车符处理问题；Cloudflare Workers中的fetch请求默认使用http；移动设备上GPS数据可能被静默移除；PostgreSQL的NOTIFY在事务中执行导致频繁写入WAL；npm脚本每次运行时会调用npm注册表，不适合健康检查；某些JavaScript开发者通过添加大量依赖实现向后兼容；bcrypt仅使用密码的前72字节；JavaScript Date对象的月份索引从0开始，而年份和日期从1开始；Node.js在特定情况下导入模块会崩溃；PostgreSQL的参数上限为65,535，影响大数据集的批量插入；一些Web功能仅在“安全上下文”中可用；TypeORM的删除操作会改变输入对象。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“被诅咒的知识”（cursed knowledge）及其在软件开发中的具体案例和处理经验的讨论。

不同观点：
• **赞赏并支持记录被诅咒的知识**：[simpaticoder]认为将被诅咒的知识记录下来并公开，不仅有助于情感宣泄，还能成为学习和预防的工具，每个项目都应具备这种机制。
• **对具体技术问题的质疑和建议**：[qdw]对一个将65k PostgreSQL占位符绑定在单个查询中的做法提出质疑，认为这是不合理的设计，并支持通过重构ORM来解决问题。他还提出将数据先加载到临时表中的方法以提高性能。
• **对多余软件包的批评**：[treve]批评某些软件包作者为了名气而导致大量带宽和磁盘空间的浪费，认为这是不必要的。
• **对npm脚本调用http的疑问**：[thorum]对npm脚本在每次运行时调用http请求进行健康检查的说法表示怀疑，并寻找其他来源验证这一说法。
• **对Cloudflare Workers默认行为的质疑**：[maxbond]对Fetch请求在Cloudflare Workers中使用http默认行为导致重定向循环的问题提出质疑，并指出文档中描述的默认行为与其遇到的实际情况不符。

补充讨论：
• **具体技术问题的经验分享**：[physicles]分享了在处理字符串代码时遇到的U+00A0非断行空格问题。[godelski]补充了关于EXIF元数据日期时间问题的讨论链接。[egruy]提到了Hadoop和Kerberos相关的技术问题及其带来的困扰。
• **对特定技术设计理由的疑问**：[hiAndrewQuinn]对bcrypt实现中仅使用字符串前72字节的设计提出疑问，质疑其合理性。
• **操作系统特定行为的讨论**：[joshdavham]分享了MacOS文件名大小写不敏感和NFC/NFD转换的问题。[burnt-resistor]列举了多个软件和操作系统中的选择退出遥测功能问题。
• **对隐私和安全处理的不同看法**：[tonyhart7]认为一个关于移动操作系统权限处理的讨论不算“被诅咒的知识”，而是合理的隐私和安全措施。[bigyabai]支持这一观点，认为这是保护机制而非诅咒。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **提议创建相关GitHub仓库**：[binary132]建议创建一个类似Awesome X的Cursed知识仓库，以汇总这些经验。
• **邀请分享更多被诅咒的知识**：[joshdavham]和其他用户鼓励分享更多被诅咒的知识，以供社区借鉴和学习。

争议焦点：
• 对某些技术设计是否合理以及是否应被视为“被诅咒的知识”存在不同看法，例如[tonyhart7]和[bigyabai]对移动操作系统权限处理的不同观点。

44831704.article_summary: 本文列出了一些在开发Immich项目过程中遇到的“诅咒”知识，即一些意外且令人困扰的技术问题。主要包括：Zitadel的自定义脚本不支持正则表达式的命名捕获组；Microsoft Entra不在其OpenID文档中包含PKCE支持，导致误解；EXIF元数据中的图像尺寸可能与实际不符；YAML的空格处理不直观；Windows隐藏文件无法用"w"标志打开；Bash脚本中的回车符处理问题；Cloudflare Workers中的fetch请求默认使用http；移动设备上GPS数据可能被静默移除；PostgreSQL的NOTIFY在事务中执行导致频繁写入WAL；npm脚本每次运行时会调用npm注册表，不适合健康检查；某些JavaScript开发者通过添加大量依赖实现向后兼容；bcrypt仅使用密码的前72字节；JavaScript Date对象的月份索引从0开始，而年份和日期从1开始；Node.js在特定情况下导入模块会崩溃；PostgreSQL的参数上限为65,535，影响大数据集的批量插入；一些Web功能仅在“安全上下文”中可用；TypeORM的删除操作会改变输入对象。
44831704.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“被诅咒的知识”（cursed knowledge）及其在软件开发中的具体案例和处理经验的讨论。

不同观点：
• **赞赏并支持记录被诅咒的知识**：[simpaticoder]认为将被诅咒的知识记录下来并公开，不仅有助于情感宣泄，还能成为学习和预防的工具，每个项目都应具备这种机制。
• **对具体技术问题的质疑和建议**：[qdw]对一个将65k PostgreSQL占位符绑定在单个查询中的做法提出质疑，认为这是不合理的设计，并支持通过重构ORM来解决问题。他还提出将数据先加载到临时表中的方法以提高性能。
• **对多余软件包的批评**：[treve]批评某些软件包作者为了名气而导致大量带宽和磁盘空间的浪费，认为这是不必要的。
• **对npm脚本调用http的疑问**：[thorum]对npm脚本在每次运行时调用http请求进行健康检查的说法表示怀疑，并寻找其他来源验证这一说法。
• **对Cloudflare Workers默认行为的质疑**：[maxbond]对Fetch请求在Cloudflare Workers中使用http默认行为导致重定向循环的问题提出质疑，并指出文档中描述的默认行为与其遇到的实际情况不符。

补充讨论：
• **具体技术问题的经验分享**：[physicles]分享了在处理字符串代码时遇到的U+00A0非断行空格问题。[godelski]补充了关于EXIF元数据日期时间问题的讨论链接。[egruy]提到了Hadoop和Kerberos相关的技术问题及其带来的困扰。
• **对特定技术设计理由的疑问**：[hiAndrewQuinn]对bcrypt实现中仅使用字符串前72字节的设计提出疑问，质疑其合理性。
• **操作系统特定行为的讨论**：[joshdavham]分享了MacOS文件名大小写不敏感和NFC/NFD转换的问题。[burnt-resistor]列举了多个软件和操作系统中的选择退出遥测功能问题。
• **对隐私和安全处理的不同看法**：[tonyhart7]认为一个关于移动操作系统权限处理的讨论不算“被诅咒的知识”，而是合理的隐私和安全措施。[bigyabai]支持这一观点，认为这是保护机制而非诅咒。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **提议创建相关GitHub仓库**：[binary132]建议创建一个类似Awesome X的Cursed知识仓库，以汇总这些经验。
• **邀请分享更多被诅咒的知识**：[joshdavham]和其他用户鼓励分享更多被诅咒的知识，以供社区借鉴和学习。

争议焦点：
• 对某些技术设计是否合理以及是否应被视为“被诅咒的知识”存在不同看法，例如[tonyhart7]和[bigyabai]对移动操作系统权限处理的不同观点。

data.title: Vibechart
data.author: datadrivenangel
data.article_summary: "Vibechart" 指的是根据个人喜好而非事实、美感或实用性来制作图表，类似于用数据可视化来传达主观偏见。这种做法类似于所谓的“谎言、该死的谎言和统计数据”的误导性。文章提到GPT-5发布时的一个图表错误，并建议人们了解图表如何说谎，还可以查看“数据可视化耻辱馆”以避免类似错误。另外，文章自嘲其网页设计（尤其是CSS动画）很差，甚至开玩笑说对手机很不友好。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI发布的图表是否存在误导性及其背后的原因

不同观点：
• **无意失误还是故意误导**：
  ◦ [sobiolite] 认为可能是疏忽导致，但仍然对一个耗费巨资的公司来说是不好的表现。
  ◦ [I_am_tiberius] 猜测可能是高层最后时刻的反馈导致了图表的调整，以夸大新模型的改进。
  ◦ [Eji1700] 认为OpenAI一向注重通过数据进行市场营销，虽非故意但懂得如何夸大结果。

• **具体图表问题**：
  ◦ [marvinborner] 指出"Coding deception"图表存在明显错误，数值50.0不应小于47.4。
  ◦ [subtlesoftware] 推测某些柱状图的高度是复制粘贴错误，但无法解释所有错误。

• **对OpenAI工作态度的质疑**：
  ◦ [atleastoptimal] 质疑OpenAI的粗心态度，怀疑是否故意制作糟糕图表以博取关注。
  ◦ [mgg90] 提到发布的游戏有简单漏洞，本可以通过额外提示修复，但依然直接发布。

• **幽默与讽刺**：
  ◦ [interweb_tube] 以幽默方式评论对图表颜色的偏好。
  ◦ [sbaidon94] 认为这种情况完美概括了当前的时代精神。
  ◦ [pryelluw] 将此问题比作Cybertruck的玻璃演示失败事件。

• **数据可视化的普遍问题**：
  ◦ [datadrivenangel] 推荐Alberto Cairo的书《How Charts Lie》，指出对误导性数据可视化的关注不应仅限于此次事件。

补充讨论：
• **对OpenAI营销策略的批评**：评论中多次提到OpenAI在数据展示上的营销策略，以及过去类似的问题（如DOTA 2时期的案例）。
• **技术演示中的问题**：提到GPT-5相关演示中存在技术漏洞，反映出发布过程中的潜在问题。

争议焦点：图表错误是由于疏忽还是故意夸大以达到营销目的。

data.title: Flipper Zero dark web firmware bypasses rolling code security
data.author: lq9AJ8yrfs
data.article_summary: YouTube频道Talking Sasquach测试了一种Flipper Zero的自定义固件，可以破解大多数现代车辆使用的滚码安全系统。这种系统通过同步算法在遥控钥匙和车辆接收器之间生成唯一代码，以防止重放攻击和未经授权的访问。与之前的RollJam攻击不同，新攻击只需捕获一次遥控钥匙信号，无需干扰，即可完全模拟钥匙的全部功能，如锁车、解锁和开启后备箱。这种攻击通过逆向工程滚码序列或利用RollBack攻击实现，使原钥匙失效。受影响车辆包括克莱斯勒、道奇、菲亚特、福特、现代、Jeep、起亚、三菱和斯巴鲁。目前尚无简单解决方案，可能需要大规模召回车辆。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：无线钥匙系统（如KeyLoq）的安全性、漏洞及其在汽车等场景中的应用。

不同观点：
• **[kj4ips]**：认为许多滚动密钥系统基于KeyLoq，该系统设计良好，但存在一个重大漏洞，即“制造商密钥”。如果该密钥泄露，通过两次样本采集即可破解序列密钥。虽然一般情况下暴力破解成本高昂，但拥有“制造商密钥”的设备可被利用来提取该密钥。

• **[RachelF]**：批评无钥匙启动功能，认为多层安全措施更好。同时提出汽车制造商可能乐见顾客车辆被盗，因为保险赔付可能带来额外销售。

• **[tzs]**：引用了新的攻击方法，指出只需一次按钮操作的捕捉即可模拟所有钥匙功能，并询问不使用钥匙是否安全。

• **[Terr_]**：建议如果信号不是广播或对人类不可见，许多攻击可以避免。例如使用门把手上的电接触或可听的声音信号。

• **[palata]**：关心钥匙失效后的后果，询问用户是否可以自行重置或需要专业帮助。

• **[antirez]**：质疑攻击是否针对KEELOQ协议，并表示对芯片中的加密技术尚未有完全破解的方法，认为需进一步理解攻击细节。

• **[gblargg]**：决定回归手动锁门并确保不将钥匙遗留在车内以避免风险。

• **[theoreticalmal]**：认为攻击可能导致原钥匙失效，攻击者可能借此制造麻烦而非直接盗车，迫使用户拖车和重新编程。

• **[tamimio]**：庆幸已拥有一个多功能钥匙，不需替换多个遥控器，并提到不容易为丢失的钥匙支付更换费用。

• **[cakealert]**：质疑为何许多汽车制造商无法正确使用加密技术。

• **[IshKebab]**：对漏洞的存在感到惊讶，怀疑实现者是否知道该漏洞。

• **[geekamongus]**：指出可以通过廉价手段获取福特车钥匙，质疑汽车安全措施的有效性。

• **[radicaldreamer]**：猜测情报机构早已知晓此类攻击。

• **[waltbosz]**：幽默表示自己早已丢失钥匙，不受此问题影响。

• **[2Gkashmiri]**：询问是否有廉价设备或DIY方案来应对该问题，提到难以购买的Flipper Zero设备。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于无线钥匙系统的安全设计漏洞及其在实际应用（如汽车）中的风险。
• 讨论中涉及了多种应对策略，包括手动操作、自行重置和购买廉价设备等。
• 有人质疑汽车制造商是否故意让车辆被盗以促进销售，这是一种阴谋论视角。
• 不同用户对漏洞的了解程度和应对方式存在差异，反映出公众对技术安全的认知差距。

44830408.article_content:
Over on YouTube Talking Sasquach has recently tested custom firmware for the Flipper Zero that can entirely break the rolling code security system used on most modern vehicles. Rolling code security works by using a synchronized algorithm between a transmitter and receiver to generate a new, unique code for each transmission, preventing replay attacks and unauthorized access.
In the past we've discussed an attack against rolling code security systems called
RollJam
, which works by jamming the original keyfob signal so the vehicle cannot receive it, and at the same time recording it for later use. However, this attack is difficult to perform in reality.
For this new attack to work, all that is needed is a single button-press capture from the keyfob, without any jamming. Just from that single capture, it is able to emulate all the keyfob's functions, including lock, unlock, and unlock trunk. A consequence of this is that the original keyfob gets out of sync, and will no longer function.
According to the Talking Sasquatch, the attack works by simply reverse engineering the rolling code sequence, either through sequence leaks or prior brute forcing of the sequence from a large list of known codes. However,
another article
mentions that the firmware is based on the "
RollBack
" attack, which works by playing back captured rolling codes in a specific order to initiate a 'rollback' of the synchronization system.
Regardless of the method, videos demonstrating the attack show that only a single capture is needed to emulate a keyfob completely.
Affected vehicles include Chrysler, Dodge, Fiat, Ford, Hyundai, Jeep, Kia, Mitsubishi and Subaru. As of yet, there appears to be no easy fix for this, other than mass vehicle recalls.

• **[gblargg]**：决定回归手动锁门并确保不将钥匙遗留在车内以避免风险。

• **[theoreticalmal]**：认为攻击可能导致原钥匙失效，攻击者可能借此制造麻烦而非直接盗车，迫使用户拖车和重新编程。

• **[tamimio]**：庆幸已拥有一个多功能钥匙，不需替换多个遥控器，并提到不容易为丢失的钥匙支付更换费用。

• **[cakealert]**：质疑为何许多汽车制造商无法正确使用加密技术。

• **[IshKebab]**：对漏洞的存在感到惊讶，怀疑实现者是否知道该漏洞。

• **[radicaldreamer]**：猜测情报机构早已知晓此类攻击。

• **[waltbosz]**：幽默表示自己早已丢失钥匙，不受此问题影响。

data.title: Hubble catches sharpest image yet of 3I/ATLAS
data.author: anigbrowl
data.article_summary: 哈勃太空望远镜拍摄到迄今为止最清晰的星际彗星3I/ATLAS的图像。这颗彗星正在穿越太阳系，哈勃的观测帮助天文学家更好地估算了其由尘埃和冰组成的彗核大小，直径约为320米至5.6公里。图像捕捉到了彗星喷发的尘埃羽流和远离彗核的尘尾。3I/ATLAS是继2017年发现的1I/ʻOumuamua和2019年发现的2I/Borisov之后，第三颗被观测到的星际访客，正以210,000公里/小时的速度穿越太阳系。预计到2025年9月前可见，之后将因靠近太阳而无法观测，并预计在2025年12月重新出现。哈勃的数据还显示，该彗星正以与距离太阳约4.8亿公里的彗星一致的速度失去尘埃。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

补充讨论：
• 该评论引出了对3I/ATLAS天体识别过程的时间线的关注，特别是它作为彗星的认定是早期就已确定还是近期发展的。这暗示了对天文事件时间线和分类变化的潜在兴趣。

(注：此评论内容较为简短，主要围绕3I/ATLAS是否早期被识别为彗星展开讨论，并未出现明确的争议或多种对立观点。)

44831843.article_content:
The Hubble Space Telescope has captured the sharpest image yet of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, which is currently passing through our Solar System.
Observations by Hubble have enabled astronomers to better estimate the size of the
comet
's nucleus, which is made of dust and ice.
Hubble managed to capture a dust plume being ejected by the comet, as well as a glimpse of a dust tail streaming away from its nucleus.
Image of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS captured by the Hubble Space Telescope’s Wide Field Camera on 21 July 2025. Credit: NASA, ESA, D. Jewitt (UCLA); Image Processing: J. DePasquale (STScI)
An interstellar visitor
3I/ATLAS
is one of only three interstellar visitors ever observed passing through our Solar System, the other two being 1I/ʻOumuamua, discovered in 2017, and 2I/Borisov, discovered in 2019.
These objects originate from deep space and make a brief detour through our Solar System, then continue on their journey across the cosmos.
Comet 3I/ATLAS (2025) was discovered by the Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System (ATLAS) on 1 July 2025, when it was 675 million kilometres from the Sun.
Hubble's image, captured on 21 July 2025, follows an earlier
Gemini North Telescope image of 3I/ATLAS
, which you can see below.
Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS as seen by the Gemini North Telescope. Credit: International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/K. Meech (IfA/U. Hawaii). Image Processing: Jen Miller & Mahdi Zamani (NSF NOIRLab)
3I/ATLAS is currently visible through telescopes and will be into September 2025, but after this time it will pass too close to the Sun to be seen from Earth.
It's expected to reappear on the other side of the Sun and be visible again in early December 2025.
3I/ATLAS is traveling through our Solar System at 210,000 kilometres per hour, making it the speediest Solar System visitor ever seen.
Astronomers say its speed suggests it's been zooming through interstellar space for billions of years, sped up by the gravitational force of stars and nebulae.
Image of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS captured by the Hubble Space Telescope’s Wide Field Camera on 21 July 2025, with scale bar. Credit: NASA, ESA, D. Jewitt (UCLA); Image Processing: J. DePasquale (STScI)
Hubble's view of 3I/ATLAS
Data on 3I/ATLAS gathered by the Hubble Space Telescope suggests it must be as wide as 5.6 kilometres at most, and at least 320 metres.
But astronomers say that, although Hubble has helped refine these estimates, the heart of the comet still cannot be seen at the moment.
It's thought that observations by other observatories like the James Webb Space Telescope will help refine what we know about the comet, including its chemical makeup.
Diagram showing the trajectory of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, or C/2025 N1, as it passes through the Solar System. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech
3I/ATLAS's dusty tail
Comets are frozen balls of dust and ice, and so when they get close to a star like our Sun, they heat up, and some of that frozen material turns into gas, streaming away from the comet.
Hubble has captured one such dust plume emerging from the side of the comet that's facing the Sun.
Data suggests 3I/ATLAS is losing dust at a rate consistent with comets that are detected around 480 million kilometres from the Sun.
Yet while the vast majority of comets that we know of originated on the outer edges of our Solar System, this interstellar visitor likely originated in some other Solar System, far beyond our Galaxy.
If you manage to capture an image of 3I/ATLAS, we'd love to see it! Send it to us via
contactus@skyatnightmagazine.com

data.title: Achieving 10,000x training data reduction with high-fidelity labels
data.author: badmonster
data.article_summary: 谷歌广告团队提出了一种新的主动学习方法，能够大幅减少微调大型语言模型（LLM）所需的训练数据量，降幅达到10,000倍。该方法通过使用零或少样本的初始模型（LLM-0）生成大量初步标签，然后对标签数据进行聚类分析，识别出最具信息量的样本对并交由专家标注。通过反复迭代，模型与人类专家的对齐度提高了65%。在生产系统中，使用更大模型时，数据量减少了四个数量级，同时保持或提升了质量。该方法不依赖于“地面真值”，而是使用Cohen’s Kappa系数来衡量模型与专家的一致性，Kappa值高于0.8被认为表现极佳。这种方法有效解决了训练数据昂贵且难以获取的问题，尤其适用于广告内容安全分类等复杂任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕点击诱饵检测、主动学习中的文本分类、嵌入和聚类方法的技术讨论

不同观点：
• [ericyd] 认为在实际生产环境中，只有很少的广告是点击诱饵，这与个人多年上网的经验不符。该评论对点击诱饵的低比例提出质疑，反映出实际感受与数据结果的差距。

• [abhgh] 指出主动学习在文本分类中的应用非常复杂，并通过与其同事的实证研究发现，随机选择实例进行标注在规范化实验设置后表现更好。这与通常认为的主动学习方法优于随机选择的做法形成对比。

• [ghm2180] 质疑使用支持向量机（SVM）选择支持向量和忽略异常值的做法，认为这种方法可能故意模糊了某些商业秘密，比如如何选择实例交给人工标注。该评论对技术透明性和具体算法选择提出疑问。

• [scribu] 对文中提到的聚类步骤感到困惑，指出既然点击诱饵和非点击诱饵的标签是分开的，怎么会产生重叠的聚类。该评论对聚类方法的合理性提出质疑，关注聚类的实际效果。

• [patresh] 关注嵌入的生成方式，质疑是否使用了除LLM外的其他模型来进行嵌入和聚类，指出LLM通常不适合直接用于这些任务。该评论强调了技术细节的透明性和方法选择的合理性。

补充讨论：
• [trhway] 提到2001年Andrew Ng’s Data-Centric AI比赛的获胜者通过分析嵌入的分离性来选择训练数据，呼应了对嵌入和数据选择方法的讨论，提供了一个历史案例以供参考。

争议焦点：
• 点击诱饵在实际流量中的比例问题，[ericyd]的个人经验与数据结果不符。
• 主动学习方法的有效性，[abhgh]的研究结果与传统观点相悖。
• 聚类方法的合理性，[scribu]对文中描述的聚类结果表示不解。
• 嵌入模型的选择和使用，[patresh]对LLM用于嵌入和聚类的适用性提出质疑。

44830418.article_content:
Achieving 10,000x training data reduction with high-fidelity labels
August 7, 2025
Markus Krause, Engineering Manager, and Nancy Chang, Research Scientist, Google Ads
A new active learning method for curating high-quality data that reduces training data requirements for fine-tuning LLMs by orders of magnitude.
Classifying unsafe ad content has proven an enticing problem space for leveraging large language models (LLMs). The inherent complexity involved in identifying policy-violating content demands solutions capable of deep contextual and cultural understanding, areas of relative strength for LLMs over traditional machine learning systems. But fine-tuning LLMs for such complex tasks requires high-fidelity training data that is difficult and expensive to curate at the necessary quality and scale. Standard data-intensive approaches to training models are costly, especially given the need to handle
concept drift
as safety policies evolve or as new types of unsafe ad content arise. In the worst case the model must be retrained on a completely new data set. Reducing the amount of training data needed is therefore paramount.
With this in mind, we describe a new, scalable curation process for
active learning
that can drastically reduce the amount of training data needed for fine-tuning LLMs while significantly improving model alignment with human experts. The process can be applied to datasets of hundreds of billions of examples to iteratively identify the examples for which annotation would be most valuable and then use the resulting expert labels for fine-tuning.
In our experiments, we were able to reduce the scale of training data needed from 100,000 to under 500 training examples, while increasing model alignment with human experts by up to 65%. Production systems using larger models have seen even greater reductions in data scale, using up to four orders of magnitude less data while maintaining or improving quality.
Curation process
Our process starts with a zero- or few-shot initial model (LLM-0), which we provide with a prompt describing the content of interest, e.g., defining clickbait and asking “Is this ad clickbait?” The LLM-0 model then labels ads as
clickbait
(orange in the figure below) or
benign
(blue) and generates a large labeled data set, shown as
(1)
below. Note that this initial data set is typically highly imbalanced, since in production traffic only very few (<1%) ads are actually clickbait. The LLM’s true positive rate is also low because it has not yet been fine-tuned. To find the most informative examples, we separately cluster examples labeled clickbait and examples labeled benign, which yields some overlapping clusters, thus indicating potential model confusion between clickbait and benign examples
(2)
. For each such overlapping cluster pair, we find pairs of examples lying nearest each other that have different labels
(3)
and send these to human experts for an opinion. If needed to stay within our review budget, we prioritize pairs of examples that cover a larger area of our search space
(4)
. The resulting curated set is both informative (since it contains the most confusable examples along the decision boundary) and diverse (since it draws from different regions along that decision boundary).
The curation process generates preliminary labels using a few-shot LLM and then clusters each label set. Overlapping clusters with differing labels are used to identify sampled pairs of examples that are both informative and diverse.
These expert-provided labels are split randomly into two sets. The first is used for model evaluation, based on two key alignment metrics: the internal alignment measuring how much experts agree, and the model–human alignment between the current model and human experts. The second is used to fine-tune the current models, producing the next iteration of the model. The process repeats until the model–human alignment either matches the internal alignment or plateaus and cannot be improved further.
Metric
Our curation process does not assume the existence of ground truth. Many classification problems in the ads safety space, such as content moderation or fraud detection, are inherently ambiguous and require interpretation and deliberation, even among policy experts. We therefore cannot rely on standard metrics like precision and recall, which require a ground truth label. Instead we use
Cohen’s Kappa
, a measure of how well two independent annotators align, above what would be expected from chance agreement. In our experiments, Cohen’s Kappa is used as both a quality indicator for datasets (including model evaluation during the curation process, as noted above); and as a measure of model performance. Values closer to 1 show higher alignment, 0 indicates no alignment above chance, and negative values indicate systematic disagreement. data.article_summary: Cursor CLI是一款终端工具，帮助开发者直接在终端中进行代码编辑和管理工作。它支持在任何IDE或终端中使用，提供一致的命令体验，并允许实时指导和自定义工作规则。开发者可以通过它审查代理编辑、直接修改代码，并集成到各种开发环境如VSCode、JetBrains等。此外，Cursor CLI提供最新的模型支持，如GPT-5和Claude-4，可用于编写脚本和自动化任务，如文档更新和安全审查。安装可通过命令行执行：`curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash`。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编码代理工具（如AGENT.md、Claude.md等）的应用与发展前景

不同观点：
• [thehamkercat] 认为所有工具最终都会采用AGENT.md，并停止使用其他类似工具（如gemini.md、claude.md等），给出了AGENT.md的相关链接。
• [amclennon] 对每周都有新的AI编码工具发布持积极态度，表示乐见其成，尤其在JavaScript框架层出不穷的背景下。
• [byronic] 质疑这些工具的实际应用场景，认为虚拟机环境可能更实用，并表示不愿意给予LLM写权限访问自己的磁盘。
• [phren0logy] 支持终端编码代理工具，认为终端工具比传统IDE更有趣且更具生产力，并预测2025年将是终端年。
• [ankit219] 提出CLI工具的未来可能是通过GitHub PRs实现自动化修复问题或功能，并指出GitHub Copilot已有类似功能，但还不够完善。
• [ribeyes] 看好Cursor工具集的长期发展，认为其在CLI、IDE、GitHub应用等方面的整合将提供端到端的开发体验，并强调应支持低切换成本和模型改进而非UI/数据锁定。
• [tsvetkov] 认为代理工具正在重新定义IDE，传统IDE UI的重要性将下降，CLI工具和MCP可能更简单、更具可组合性和可移植性。

补充讨论：
• [LeoPanthera] 希望Anthropic能推出“Claude GUI”。
• [lherron] 质疑Cursor产品的生存空间，认为在已有OAI/Anthropic/GOOG等订阅服务的情况下，额外付费不划算。
• [unsupp0rted] 对CLI工具相比传统IDE的优势提出疑问。
• [cheema33] 指出Claude Code的手动验证和自动化需求，认为Cursor CLI能解决其痛点。
• [risho] 对工具的反馈和可视化不足提出问题，希望工具能更具可操作性和透明度。
• [cyounkins] 希望比较Cursor与Claude Code和aider的功能。
• [lvl155] 批评Cursor只是对其他工具的包装，缺乏原创性。
• [kamatour] 调侃大家都在等待AGENT.md成为新的README标准。

争议焦点：
• 工具的实际应用价值与传统IDE的比较。
• Cursor产品的生存空间与竞争优势。
• 工具的反馈机制和用户体验问题。

data.title: AST-Driven Python Testing
data.author: MarcoDewey
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用大型语言模型（LLM）生成模糊测试（fuzz test）的合理性

不同观点：
• Jtsummers认为，相比于使用LLM生成20个模糊测试，采用传统的模糊测试工具可能更全面。这些工具结合灰盒（grey-box）和白盒（white-box）技术，执行起来可能更便宜且更快。
• 潜在反对观点（隐含）：有人可能认为LLM生成模糊测试具有灵活性和适应性，尤其在处理复杂或新颖的代码结构时，能够提供一种快速生成测试用例的方法。

补充讨论：
• Jtsummers强调了传统模糊测试工具在全面性和效率上的优势，尤其是在结合灰盒和白盒技术的情况下，可能在测试覆盖率和执行速度上优于LLM生成的测试。
• 讨论焦点在于测试的全面性和效率之间的权衡，以及不同工具在实际应用中的适用性。
• LLM生成测试的价值可能在于其在特定场景下的快速原型设计和灵活性，而传统模糊测试工具的优势则体现在长期和全面的测试过程中。

data.title: 79% of OpenBSD kernel source is AMD DRM
data.author: cnst
data.article_summary: 作者H. Hartzer在邮件中指出，在OpenBSD系统中，解压后的源码文件大小约为1.7GB，而其中sys/dev/pci/drm/amd目录占据了499MB，其下的include子目录占据了458MB。他质疑这些文件的大小是否必要，是否可以进行精简。Hartzer认为该目录的大小显得过于庞大。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenBSD 7.9内核源代码中AMD DRM占据大部分体积，讨论现代操作系统中GPU驱动相关问题。

不同观点：
• [cnst] 指出OpenBSD 7.9内核源代码的634MB中，79%的体积来自AMD的Direct Rendering Manager (DRM) 实现，尤其是asic_reg目录。并对比Linux内核中类似情况，强调这是源代码体积，而非编译后的代码。还指出OpenBSD 6.5到7.7版本之间，内核源码体积的急剧增长。

• [bombcar] 认为现代计算机实际上是以GPU为中心，CPU和操作系统只是辅助启动和支持GPU运行。这一观点呼应了内核源码中DRM占据大量体积的现象。

• [somat] 部分理解这种现象，指出没有稳定的指令集架构（ISA）使得硬件厂商可以创新，但也导致每个硬件设备几乎都需要独特的驱动。尽管对AMD的开源态度表示赞赏，但也希望AMD能清理驱动代码或确定一个稳定的ISA。

• [methou] 提醒Mac和Windows用户不要将Direct Rendering Manager (DRM) 与数字版权管理（Digital Rights Management）混淆，提供了相关维基百科链接以澄清概念。

• [__turbobrew__] 简单地表示AMD的代码是“臃肿的”（bloat）。

• [snvzz] 认为GPU驱动应该放在用户空间，而不是内核中，但指出由于UNIX架构的历史原因，目前仍然难以摆脱这种设计。

补充讨论：
• [rasz] 提供了一个相关链接，提到Linux内核维护者曾拒绝了一个AMDGPU补丁，暗示在Linux社区中也存在对AMD驱动代码的争议。

争议焦点：
• 内核中包含大量GPU驱动代码是否合理，尤其是AMD DRM实现占据了OpenBSD内核源码的绝大部分。
• 是否应该将GPU驱动移到用户空间，以减少内核的复杂性和体积。
• AMD驱动代码的“臃肿”问题以及是否需要一个更稳定的ISA以减少设备特异性驱动的问题。

data.author: zoidb
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同编程语言在代码可靠性和开发效率上的比较，特别是C语言与Rust语言的对比。

不同观点：
• 观点一：支持Rust语言，认为其编译器能够捕捉到错误，从而提高代码的可靠性，减少对复杂测试和自定义编码模式的依赖。Rust在这方面比C语言更具优势，可能吸引那些追求更高可靠性的开发者。

• 观点二：暗示对C语言的偏好，提到有人（暗指"she"）可能因为个人喜好而继续使用C语言，即使Rust在可靠性方面可能更优。这表明对某种语言的习惯或个人偏好可能影响开发者选择，而不单单是技术优势。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到Rust不需要"clever coding patterns"和自定义包装器（wrappers），表明Rust在设计上更注重安全和简化开发过程，这可能是其相较于C语言的一个显著优点。
• 提到“come around”暗示了一种预期或等待时间的问题，即Rust的优点可能需要时间才能被广泛接受和认可。
• 争议的焦点在于开发者对编程语言的选择是基于个人偏好还是技术优势，这可能会影响语言的普及和接受度。

data.title: High costs and thin margins threatening AI coding startups
data.author: spenvo
data.article_summary: Windsurf曾计划以约30亿美元的估值出售给OpenAI，但交易失败。尽管Windsurf增长迅速并吸引风投，但因使用大型语言模型（LLM）的成本高昂，其毛利率非常低，甚至为负。AI编码助手业务竞争激烈，供应商如Anthropic和OpenAI也在直接竞争。Windsurf本可自行开发模型以降低成本，但这一策略风险高且耗资巨大。类似压力可能也影响其他公司如Anysphere。Anysphere拒绝收购提议，并计划开发自有模型，同时期待LLM成本下降。然而，最新AI模型的成本不降反升，未来变化尚不明朗。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同评论者对科技公司运营模式、成本结构及其市场策略的看法，特别是围绕Anysphere/Cursor和Anthropic等公司。

不同观点：
• [v5v3] 指出文章中提到的公司名称Anysphere实际上是Cursor的曾用名，并提供了相关链接以帮助其他读者理解背景。该评论者关注的是文章中公司名称的混淆问题，并主动查证后给出解释。

• [ankit219] 讨论了Anthropic公司在最新一轮融资中公布的毛利率（约60%），并与其他公司（如Cursor）进行对比。他认为Anthropic通过较高的毛利率可以在不亏损的情况下提供更多的服务（如更多的tokens），而其他初创公司如果基于相同的假设运营可能会面临困境。他还指出Anthropic在近一年内没有降价，暗示其定价策略相对稳定。

• [techpineapple] 提出了一种不同的观点，认为公司不应该在开发新工艺或新产品时，利用投资资金以亏损价格销售产品，除非是清仓情况。他担心这种以亏损价格销售的模式可能会导致市场不公平竞争，并认为这种做法不应被法律允许。

补充讨论：
• [ankit219] 的评论中提到了行业内常见的毛利率计算方式，特别是如何处理免费用户的相关成本，并将其归入客户获取成本（cac）或研发（r&d）中。这一细节揭示了科技公司如何通过成本分摊优化财务表现。

• [techpineapple] 的观点引发了对市场竞争和法律监管的讨论，特别是关于定价策略的合法性问题，这与其他评论者的关注点形成了对比——其他评论者更关注实际的运营数据和市场策略，而非法律或道德问题。

争议焦点：科技公司是否应该以亏损价格销售产品以获取市场份额，以及这种做法是否应该受到法律限制。这是[techpineapple]与其他评论者（如[ankit219]）潜在的立场分歧。

44831837.article_content:
In February, AI coding startup Windsurf was in talks to raise a big new round at a
$2.85 billion valuation led by Kleiner Perkins
, at double the valuation it hit six months earlier, sources told TechCrunch at the time. That deal didn’t happen, according to a source familiar with the matter. Instead, news broke in April that the startup planned to sell itself to OpenAI for roughly the same valuation:
$3 billion
.
While that deal famously fell apart, one bigger question remains: If the startup was growing that fast and attracting VC interest, why would it sell at all?
Insiders tell TechCrunch that for all the popularity and hype around AI coding assistants, they can actually be massively money-losing businesses. Vibe coders generally, and Windsurf in particular, can have such expensive structures that their gross margins are “very negative,” one person close to Windsurf told TechCrunch. Meaning it cost more to run the product than the startup could charge for it.
This is due to the high costs of using large language models (LLMs), the person explained. AI coding assistants are particularly pressured to always offer the most recent, most advanced, and most expensive LLMs because model makers are particularly fine-tuning their latest models for improvements in coding and related tasks like debugging.
This is a challenge compounded by fierce competition in the vibe-coding and code-assist market. Rivals include companies that already have huge customer bases like Anysphere’s Cursor and GitHub Copilot.
The most straightforward path to improving margins in this business involves the startups building their own models, thereby eliminating costs of paying suppliers like Anthropic and OpenAI.
“It’s a very expensive business to run if you’re not going to be in the model game,” said the person.

But that idea comes with its own risks. Windsurf’s co-founder and CEO, Varun Mohan, ultimately decided against the company building its own model — an expensive undertaking, the person said.
In addition, model makers are already competing directly. Anthropic offers Claude Code and OpenAI offers Codex, for instance.
Selling the business was a strategic move to lock in a high return before it could be undermined by the very companies that supplied its AI, including OpenAI and Anthropic, which were also entering the AI coding market.
Multiple people believe that the same pressure on margins Windsurf faced could be impacting Anysphere, the maker of Cursor, as well as vibe coders like Lovable, Replit, and others.
“Margins on all of the ‘code gen’ products are either neutral or negative. They’re absolutely abysmal,” said Nicholas Charriere, founder of Mocha, a vibe-coding startup and back-end hosting solution serving small and medium businesses (SMBs). He added that he believes the variable costs for all the startups in the sector are very close, likely within 10% to 15% of one another.
Unlike Windsurf, Anysphere has been growing so fast that it intends to remain an independent company, having already
turned down acquisition offers
, including, reports say, from OpenAI.
And Anysphere
announced in January
that it is attempting to build its own model, which could give it more control over its expenses.
In July, the startup
hired two leaders from Anthropic’s Claude Code
team, the Information reported, but two weeks later, these employees
returned
to work at Anthropic.
In addition to building a model, Anysphere could expect the cost of LLMs to decrease over time.
“That’s what everyone’s banking on,” said Erik Nordlander, a general partner at Google Ventures. “The inference cost today, that’s the most expensive it’s ever going to be.”
It’s not entirely clear how true that is. Rather than falling as expected, the
cost of some of the latest AI models has risen
, as they use more time and computational resources to handle complicated, multistep tasks.
When that will change remains to be seen. On Thursday, for instance,
OpenAI introduced
a new flagship model, GPT-5, with fees that are significantly less than its competitor, Anthropic’s Claude Opus

data.title: Eggs are off the hook–study reveals bacon's the real heart risk
data.author: bookmtn
data.article_summary: 一项由南澳大学进行的突破性研究表明，鸡蛋并非如长久以来认为的那样是导致高胆固醇的饮食罪魁祸首。实际上，升高有害低密度脂蛋白（LDL）胆固醇水平的主要因素是饱和脂肪，而非鸡蛋中的胆固醇。研究发现，每天食用两个鸡蛋，作为低饱和脂肪饮食的一部分，甚至可以帮助降低LDL胆固醇水平，挑战了过时的饮食指南。因此，鸡蛋对心脏健康无害，而像培根和香肠这类高饱和脂肪食物才是真正的风险。这项研究为鸡蛋正名，并建议人们在享用鸡蛋时避免搭配高饱和脂肪的配餐。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：饮食中的胆固醇与血液中胆固醇的关系以及对饮食习惯的态度

不同观点：
• [amanaplanacanal] 认为关于饮食中的胆固醇不影响血液中的胆固醇水平这一观点并不是新发现，质疑新闻中的所谓"新信息"是否有实际新意。
• [Igrom] 用讽刺的语气暗示人们一直在与像培根这样的高胆固醇食物“作战”，可能是在表达对饮食建议变化的无奈或不信任。
• [dlachausse] 表示无论怎样宣传饮食胆固醇的危害，自己都不会放弃吃培根，甚至愿意为此承担健康风险，暗示对培根的强烈偏好。
• [bamboozled] 以讽刺的语调预测未来可能会把其他食物（如鸡蛋）当作健康问题的替罪羊，暗示对未来饮食建议变化的怀疑和不信任。

补充讨论：
• 评论中反映出公众对饮食建议不断变化的困惑和怀疑，特别是对高胆固醇食物如培根的态度分歧。
• 存在一定的争议焦点，即饮食中的胆固醇是否真正影响健康，以及个人是否愿意为了饮食偏好而承担健康风险。
• 评论中还隐含了对科学研究和健康建议不断变化的调侃和不信任感。

Science News

Eggs are off the hook—study reveals bacon’s the real heart risk
Date:
July 28, 2025
Source:
University of South Australia
Summary:
Eggs are finally being vindicated after decades of cholesterol-related blame. New research from the University of South Australia reveals that eggs, despite their cholesterol content, aren't the dietary villains they've long been made out to be. Instead, it's the saturated fats found in foods like bacon and sausage that actually elevate harmful LDL cholesterol levels. In a world-first study, researchers showed that eating two eggs a day, as part of a low saturated fat diet, can even help reduce LDL cholesterol, challenging outdated guidelines and offering heart-healthy news for breakfast lovers everywhere.
Share:
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
LinkedIN
Email
FULL STORY
A world-first study has cracked the egg myth wide open: cholesterol in eggs doesn’t raise bad cholesterol. It’s saturated fat that does. So go ahead—have your eggs, just skip the bacon. Credit: Shutterstock
From poached to panfried, when it comes to eggs, it's all sunny side up, as new research from the University of South Australia confirms that this breakfast favourite won't crack your cholesterol.
Long blamed for high cholesterol, eggs have been beaten up for their assumed role in cardiovascular disease (CVD). Now, UniSA researchers have shown definitively that it's not dietary cholesterol in eggs but the saturated fat in our diets that's the real heart health concern.
In a world-first study, researchers examined the independent effects of dietary cholesterol and saturated fat on LDL cholesterol (the 'bad' kind), finding that eating two eggs a day - as part of a high cholesterol but low saturated fat diet - can actually reduce LDL levels and lower the risk of heart disease.
CVD is the leading cause of death worldwide, responsible for nearly 18 million deaths each year. In Australia, one person dies from CVD every 12 minutes, accounting for one in four of deaths nationwide.
Lead researcher, UniSA's Professor Jon Buckley, says it's time to rethink the reputation of eggs.
"Eggs have long been unfairly cracked by outdated dietary advice," Prof Buckley says.
"They're unique - high in cholesterol, yes, but low in saturated fat. Yet it's their cholesterol level that has often caused people to question their place in a healthy diet.
"In this study, we separated the effects of cholesterol and saturated fat, finding that high dietary cholesterol from eggs, when eaten as part of a low saturated fat diet, does not raise bad cholesterol levels.
"Instead, it was the saturated fat that was the real driver of cholesterol elevation.
"You could say we've delivered hard-boiled evidence in defense of the humble egg.
"So, when it comes to a cooked breakfast, it's not the eggs you need to worry about - it's the extra serve of bacon or the side of sausage that's more likely to impact your heart health."

data.title: The Bus Station That Didn't Exist, and Other Data Epiphanies
data.author: edent
data.article_summary:
本文作者拥有20年跨领域的数据工作经验，强调数据素养不仅在于技术能力，还在于挑战对数据的假设、评估其适用性和伦理。作者分享了两个关键案例：

1. **数据定义不准确**：在COVID期间，作者发现官方公交站数据集未包含一个重要的公交车站（Turnpike Lane），因为数据集仅记录了“公交站点”而非“公交车站”，导致无法满足特定需求。这反映了数据定义和采集过程中的不足。

2. **数据缺失或不完整**：作者提到W.E.B. Du Bois在缺乏数据情况下自行收集，完成了著名的信息图项目。类似地，在疫情期间，作者尝试用不完整的数据（如Google Places的“繁忙时间”）来估算人行道密度，取得了一定成效。在另一个项目中，作者发现皮肤病图像数据本身存在偏见，无法训练出无偏的AI模型。

作者强调，数据拥有者应思考数据是否全面，并考虑扩展其用途，同时反思数据缺失背后的问题。

44808232.article_content:
“Data is multidisciplinary” is my mantra—it’s 2025, and I’ve now worked 20 years in every possible flavour of data—data visualization, open data advocacy, data pipelines in healthcare, data-driven national-scale services, AI innovation, and more. Whatever the application or project, my take on data literacy is the fundamental ability to challenge your own assumptions about the data you have or don’t, the appropriateness in using it, the ethics of your application, and ask yourself: is there a different way, perhaps? Here is a gallery of some of my most treasured eureka moments working with data.
You have a clear purpose but the data isn’t quite right for it
I regularly walk through the Turnpike Lane Bus Station, there’s a pretty big sign pointing to it. It’s a major node for North London public transport and yet, a few years back, I found out that it did not exist… in the data, at least. I used to run the official data set of bus stops for the UK Government—a rather obscure dataset that made its way into powering a few popular journey planners like Google Maps and City Mapper.
This was 2020 during COVID, and one of my colleagues wanted a list of all bus stations in the country in order to send posters which advertised social distancing. While the dataset contained over 500,000 points, it did not contain this bus station. The problem data definitions: the dataset listed bus stops, which were not the same things as bus stations. While the words “bus station” have a common sense meaning in our minds as a collection of bus stops, that meaning was not translated into the dataset. The individual bus stops making the bus station are all in the datasets, except there was no way to group them together other than trying to
infer
they’re part of the same bus station because of their proximity.
I found other interesting issues in the dataset. Some were easy to spot, like bus stations in the middle of the North Sea. Other stations were a few meters away from their real location, which would not have a huge impact unless we were trying to use the dataset to get self-driving buses to park automatically. So, why weren’t these groupings captured in the first place? The process that created and populated the data never asked itself “are we capturing everything that we need about this bus stop?”. As a result, the dataset wasn’t quite fit for the purpose we were looking to deliver. The translated definitions of common sense concepts into data is a major element of making sure that a dataset is usable and stays current, and having a process that allows that question to emerge is an ingredient of good data management. At the time, to my surprise, we didn’t have either.
Disappointingly, data that may appear suitable to your purpose is not always; and if you are in the fortunate position of being the owner of a dataset, always ask: are there any use cases that would be out of scope for this dataset, and is it worth expanding?
Image credit: Giuseppe Sollazzo
Sometimes the data is really incomplete or missing
W.E.B. Du Bois is widely remembered for his infographics about the conditions of African Americans at the end of the nineteenth century. What I always hail him for was having shown that a lack of data should not stop a good data project and that sometimes the hard work is putting data together. When he realised the US Census lacked data about African Americans, he assembled his own survey and team,collecting data that resulted in his now famous infographics. Incomplete or missing data is something that I’ve regularly had to cope with and decide whether to pursue the initial project or pivot to something different. Once again, during the pandemic, we were trying to see if there was a way to check the density of people on pavements, and entered a tunnel trying to find the accurate measurements of pavements for the whole of the UK—an impossible task. This is when I realised using a
proxy
would have given informative enough results, as did The Economist in the chart below, created by collecting, over time, Google Places “busy times” for major points of interest in major cities. Simple, effective, but not based on anywhere close to “complete” data.
Source:
The Economist
Sometimes missing data should make us reflect. In one of my projects while working for public healthcare in the UK, a team of dermatologists came asking if my team could develop an AI algorithm to grade a type of skin condition. The intent was very positive: in their clinical research, they realised human medics were biased, resulting in less accurate grading for people who are not white, and were looking for AI to help correct that bias. 本文作者拥有20年跨领域的数据工作经验，强调数据素养不仅在于技术能力，还在于挑战对数据的假设、评估其适用性和伦理。作者分享了两个关键案例：

1. **数据定义不准确**：在COVID期间，作者发现官方公交站数据集未包含一个重要的公交车站（Turnpike Lane），因为数据集仅记录了“公交站点”而非“公交车站”，导致无法满足特定需求。这反映了数据定义和采集过程中的不足。

2. **数据缺失或不完整**：作者提到W.E.B. Du Bois在缺乏数据情况下自行收集，完成了著名的信息图项目。类似地，在疫情期间，作者尝试用不完整的数据（如Google Places的“繁忙时间”）来估算人行道密度，取得了一定成效。在另一个项目中，作者发现皮肤病图像数据本身存在偏见，无法训练出无偏的AI模型。

作者强调，数据拥有者应思考数据是否全面，并考虑扩展其用途，同时反思数据缺失背后的问题。

主要讨论点：关于某国将服役人员提前开除是否合理及其影响的讨论

不同观点：
• horns4lyfe认为，直接将服役人员开除是愚蠢且不友善的行为，但同时指出，按规定服役20年才能退休，因此如果他们在未满20年时自愿离开，本来也不应获得退休福利，所以有关退休的讨论具有一定误导性。
  
• rhelz强烈反对这种做法，认为因为政治原因否认服役人员的退休权利是极其不公正的。他们质疑为什么有人会为这样一个国家辩护，因为该国可能会基于任意政治动机剥夺他们的退休福利。

• techpineapple从另一个角度切入，提到之前有报道称乌克兰为了增加军队人数，推动了对LGBTQ+群体的包容政策，但现在军方在招募困难的情况下，选择减少包容性可能不是明智的解决方案。他们认为这种决策最终会使美国人更不安全。

• ungreased0675的观点较为简明，认为如果服役人员没有服满规定的年限，就不应获得退休资格，强调了制度本身的规则。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于提前开除服役人员的正当性以及这种行为是否会导致不公平的退休福利剥夺。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是决策的政治背景及其对社会包容性的影响，尤其是在军队招募困难的情况下，政策的调整可能带来的负面效应。
- 讨论还涉及到此类决策是否会对国家安全产生长远影响，比如techpineapple提到的情况。

data.author: janandonly
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了特瑞·吉列姆的科幻经典电影《巴西》在近四十年后依然具有预见性，尤其是对残酷官僚制度的描绘。电影开篇因一只苍蝇导致的姓氏打字错误，使得无辜的布托被误认为恐怖分子，反映了政府的无责任感和官僚主义。在2025年重看这部电影，其对极权和无效率官僚体系的讽刺依然与当今政治环境产生共鸣。影片通过艺术装饰风格的城市景观和纳粹象征的场景，营造出一种令人毛骨悚然的氛围。主角萨姆·洛瑞是一个不求上进的普通官僚，在追逐纠正错误的过程中，遭遇各部门的互相推诿，反映了无道德的职业主义和自我利益。文章还提到2023年美国移民和海关执法局的类似错误，呼应了《巴西》对政府失责的讽刺。

40 years later, Brazil is as prescient as ever
It isn’t the technology of Terry Gilliam’s sci-fi classic that holds up, but the film’s depiction of cruel bureaucracy.
It isn’t the technology of Terry Gilliam’s sci-fi classic that holds up, but the film’s depiction of cruel bureaucracy.
by
Kevin Nguyen

See All by
Kevin Nguyen
is a features editor at The Verge, where he publishes award-winning stories about labor, business, and policing. Previously, he was a senior editor at GQ.
Brazil
opens with a bureaucratic error. A fly gets stuck in a typewriter, changing the surname of Archibald Tuttle to Archibald Buttle, a misprint on a form that dictates the government forcibly detain a suspected terrorist (Tuttle) but instead leads to the arrest of an entirely innocent man (Buttle). If the inciting events of our great science fiction films have been hostile aliens, seductive robots, and reckless technologies, Terry Gilliam begins his with a humble typo.
Rewatching
Brazil
in 2025 — nearly four decades after its release — it’s hard to understate how well this movie holds up. Wildly inventive at every turn, Gilliam’s satirical vision of a cruel and violent bureaucracy rings eerily true of this political moment. The film finishes a weeklong run at New York’s Film Forum with a new 4K restoration,
which you can also get on Blu-ray
. (And honestly, the non-4K version of
Brazil
that you can perennially stream on The Criterion Channel still looks great too.)
A lot of that has to do with Gilliam’s hysterical dystopia —
Mad Men
by way of
Wolfenstein
.
Brazil
also imagines a hyper-efficient future that never made the leap to digital. Pneumatic tubes shoot paperwork between offices; seas of typists clack forward the cogs of an industrial machine. Everything in this world is an Orwellian/Kafkaesque melange of forms and stamps and obtuse processes.
The experience of watching
Brazil
is at once being impressed by how it looks while also being horrified by what’s depicted. The ominous cityscapes have wonderfully art deco touches, yet the gargantuan buildings cast long, haunting shadows; many of the sets take inspiration from Nazi iconography, complete with gigantic eagles and massive lobbies guarded by stormtroopers. Also, look at this logo:
Isn’t that the best movie logo you’ve ever seen?
A perfectly cast Jonathan Pryce inhabits Sam Lowry, a mid-level bureaucrat. He lives in a small apartment, complete with dysfunctional Rube Goldberg gadgetry that ends up pouring coffee on his toast. (The film has no shortage of Gilliam’s adoration of slapstick, a carryover of his
Monty Python
days.) Lowry’s mother and friends push him to be more ambitious. Yet he resists the rat race, turning down a promotion to a much more prestigious branch of the government simply because he isn’t interested. In this dystopian world, oppressed by the hierarchical structures of capitalism, the only hero is a slouch.
A fantastical/horny dream plotline is the most Lowry gets activated, and as he chases down the culprit for the Tuttle and Buttle mix-up, he encounters several different departments foisting the blame off on other offices. “Information Transit got the wrong man. I got the
right
man,” says one bureaucrat. “The wrong one was delivered to me as the right man; I accepted him on good faith as the right man. Was I wrong?” There is no accountability in this government, and characters act with self-interested careerism in mind over any semblance of morality. After Buttle is killed, Lowry has to deliver a receipt to his widow.
Earlier this year, as part of the Trump administration’s attempt to deport undocumented immigrants, ICE illegally deported Kilmar Abrego Garcia. He was sent to El Salvador before the government admitted it had made an error. Then the agency backtracked, claiming it had never made a mistake. In response to calls to return Garcia to the US, the Department of Homeland Security
claimed it had no authority to do so
.
The deflection of responsibility, the ludicrous reasoning, the deferential loyalty to the state — these are the things Terry Gilliam satirized in
Braz

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特斯拉的Dojo项目及其相关前景、公司内部问题以及市场反应

不同观点：
• TheAlchemist认为特斯拉CEO埃隆·马斯克经常说谎，并提到两年前一位“领先的特斯拉分析师”预测Dojo项目将为特斯拉带来6000亿美元的价值增长。TheAlchemist指出马斯克在最近的投资者电话会议上声称Dojo明年将达到10万个H100的规模，但他对人们仍然相信马斯克表示怀疑，认为特斯拉正在快速衰落。

• cosmicgadget提到特斯拉今年面临关键人才外流的问题，并列举了几位离职的高管，如Optimus工程主管Milan Kovac和软件工程副总裁David Lau。他还质疑人才流失的原因，是由于财务紧缩还是因为受到其他机会的吸引或因马斯克的政治活动导致反感而离开。

• paxys以讽刺的口吻指出，无论特斯拉是建设还是解散Dojo超级计算机，其股票都会上涨，暗示市场对特斯拉相关消息的反应存在不合理性。

• toomuchtodo提供了一个存档链接，但未发表明确观点，可能旨在提供信息以支持其他讨论。

• techpineapple猜测，特斯拉可能将GPU资源转移到X.AI，暗示Dojo项目或其资源可能被重新分配到其他领域，如人工智能研究。

• jeffbee以幽默的方式建议开发一个浏览器扩展，分析Hacker News（HN）上的帖子，为那些曾经相信Dojo存在的人加上“再次上当”的徽章，暗示对Dojo项目真实性的怀疑。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对Dojo项目的真实性和前景存在争议，TheAlchemist和jeffbee明显表示怀疑，而cosmicgadget和techpineapple则分别关注公司内部问题和资源分配的可能性。
• 市场对特斯拉消息的反应被paxys质疑，暗示股市对特斯拉相关新闻的反应可能存在不理性和过度预期。
• 讨论还涉及特斯拉内部的人才流失问题，cosmicgadget特别提到几位关键高管的离职及其可能原因。

data.title: In a World of Hype, GraphQL's Fundamental Advantages over tRPC Still Hold True
data.author: pgte
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了tRPC和GraphQL两种API技术的优缺点，重点比较了它们在类型安全性和查询灵活性方面的表现。tRPC提供端到端类型安全和简化的代码，适合快速开发和类型安全要求高的场景，但其查询由服务器预定义，导致客户端灵活性不足，每次数据需求变化可能都需要修改服务器端代码。相比之下，GraphQL允许客户端自定义查询，灵活性更高，可以精确获取所需数据，减少冗余数据传输，且通过工具如graphql-codegen也能实现类型安全。虽然tRPC在开发速度上占优，但GraphQL在应用扩展性和团队独立性方面更具优势。选择哪种技术应根据项目需求权衡速度和灵活性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：tRPC与GraphQL的优劣比较，重点在于开发者体验与架构灵活性

不同观点：
• 观点一：tRPC具有优秀的开发者体验和端到端类型安全。tRPC的支持者认为其提供了强大的类型安全性和简洁的开发流程，减少了前后端之间的不一致问题，特别是在小型项目或团队中，开发效率显著提高。

• 观点二：GraphQL在客户端查询定制方面具备独特的架构灵活性。GraphQL的拥护者强调，其最大优势在于客户端可以根据需求定制查询，减少不必要的数据传输，这在需要高灵活性和可扩展性的项目中尤为重要。

• 观点三：GraphQL的灵活性在复杂系统中仍然具有显著优势。有人指出，在处理复杂数据需求和多变的前端需求时，GraphQL的架构优势不可忽视，特别是它能有效解决版本控制和数据获取粒度的问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于项目需求和规模对技术选择的影响。一些人认为，tRPC在小项目或快速开发中表现优异，而GraphQL更适合需要长期维护和扩展的复杂应用。

• 例子和论据：支持GraphQL的一方常提到在大型企业级应用中，如Facebook，GraphQL已经被证明能有效处理复杂的查询和数据需求。而支持tRPC的一方则以小型初创公司和快速迭代的项目为例，展示其在开发速度和类型安全方面的优势。

• 总体来看，讨论强调了根据具体项目需求选择合适技术的重要性，而不是单纯比较技术的优劣。

44829640.article_content:
It seems like
tRPC
is all the rage these days, and I get it. The promise of end-to-end type safety with minimal boilerplate code is compelling, especially for teams working within a TypeScript monorepo. It solves a real problem and makes for a great developer experience. But as a software engineer who’s been in the trenches, I can’t help but feel that the current hype often overlooks some significant disadvantages.
For me,
GraphQL
still holds a powerful and often misunderstood advantage that goes beyond the language-agnostic nature of its APIs. While that’s a huge benefit for cross-platform teams, my work is primarily web-focused, so I’m more interested in what it offers within a single application.
The Core Advantage: Client-Side Query Customization
The core advantage, in my opinion, is the ability to customize queries on the client. With tRPC, the API is essentially a collection of predefined function calls. The server dictates what data you can fetch with each call. While you get type safety, you lose flexibility.
The tRPC Approach: Server-Defined Queries
// tRPC: Server defines the available data shapes.
// The client calls a specific procedure and receives the predefined data.
const
user
=
await
trpc.users.getUser.
query
({ id:
"123"
});
// You receive the full `User` object as defined by the server.
// To get a different data shape (e.g., user with posts), a new server-side procedure is often required.
If a new UI component needs a slightly different subset of data, you often have to modify the server-side resolver or create a new one entirely. This tight coupling between the client and server can lead to over-fetching or under-fetching and makes the frontend team dependent on the backend team for every minor data requirement change.
The GraphQL Approach: Client-Defined Queries
# GraphQL: Client defines exactly what it needs
query
ProductDetail
(
$id
:
ID
!
) {
product
(
id
:
$id
) {
name
price
description
}
}
query
ProductCheckout
(
$id
:
ID
!
) {
product
(
id
:
$id
) {
name
price
# No description needed for checkout
}
}
In contrast, GraphQL puts the power of data fetching directly in the hands of the client. With a single endpoint, I can craft the exact query I need for any given component. This is incredibly useful even on the same app. Imagine an e-commerce site where the product detail page needs the product’s name, price, and description, but the checkout page only needs the name and price. With GraphQL, you simply write a different query for each component, fetching only the data you need. This not only reduces the payload size but also decouples your frontend from your backend’s implementation details.
Achieving Type Safety Without Sacrificing Flexibility
I’ve been using tools like
urql
on the client, which provides a highly customizable and flexible GraphQL experience. The ecosystem around GraphQL, including tools like
graphql-codegen
, allows me to achieve that same end-to-end type safety that tRPC champions.
Type Safety with GraphQL Code Generation
import
{ useQuery }
from
"urql"
;
import
{
ProductDetailDocument,
ProductDetailQuery,
}
from
"../generated/graphql"
;
// Fully typed queries with urql
const
[
result
]
=
useQuery
({
query: ProductDetailDocument,
variables: { id:
"123"
},
});
// result.data is fully typed as ProductDetailQuery
const
product
=
result.data?.product;
// Fully typed!
How does TypeScript know the return type?
The type safety comes from
GraphQL code generation
. Here’s how it works:
Schema Introspection
: Tools like
graphql-codegen
read your GraphQL schema and understand the exact shape of your data.
Query Analysis
: They analyze your GraphQL queries to know exactly what fields you’re requesting.
Type Generation
: They generate TypeScript interfaces and document objects that match your queries exactly.
The key is that
the generated types match your queries exactly
- if you change your GraphQL query, the TypeScript types are regenerated to match.
By generating the client types directly from my GraphQL schema and operations, my application is just as robust and bug-resistant as a tRPC one, but with the added flexibility of client-side query customization.
The Trade-off: Speed vs. Scalability
💡 Key Insight
: tRPC is great for fast iteration, but GraphQL provides architectural flexibility that pays dividends as your application grows.
The tRPC approach is great for fast-paced, tightly-coupled development, but it comes at the cost of flexibility and long-term scalability. For me, the ability to define my data requirements directly from the client is a fundamental architectural advantage that I’m not willing to give up.
When to Choose Each Approach
Aspect
tRPC
GraphQL
Development Speed
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
⭐⭐⭐
Type Safety
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Query Flexibility
⭐⭐
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Team Independence
⭐⭐
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Learning Curve
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
⭐⭐⭐
The GraphQL ecosystem has matured to the point where end-to-end type safety is a solved problem, and the flexibility it provides is a feature, not a bug.

data.title: Worktrees: Git's best kept secret (and why you should use them)
data.author: handfuloflight
data.article_summary:
Git工作树（worktrees）是Git中一个鲜为人知的强大功能，自2015年起就存在。工作树允许在一个仓库中拥有多个工作目录，每个目录可以指向不同的分支，从而简化分支切换和管理。相比传统工作流需要暂存、切换分支、修复问题再恢复工作的方式，工作树只需通过目录切换即可完成这些操作，不影响当前未提交的工作。

使用工作树的优势包括：更方便地进行代码审查、维护不同版本的代码库、处理长时间运行的测试或构建任务等。基本命令包括`git worktree add [path] [branch]`（创建新工作树）、`git worktree remove [path]`（删除工作树）和`git worktree list`（列出所有工作树）。

注意事项包括：不要在一个工作树内创建另一个工作树，以免造成混乱。通过合理使用工作树，开发者可以显著提升工作效率。

44830480.article_content:
Worktrees: Git's best kept secret (and why you should use them)
Published:
Apr 30, 2024
Table of contents
Open Table of contents
Intro
You are already using worktrees
What is actually a worktree?
Worktree based workflow vs typical workflow
Worktrees commands
Better ways to work with worktrees
How NOT to use worktrees
Worktrees level 1: project folder
Worktrees level 2: bare repo
Caveats of worktrees
A branch can only be checked out in a single worktree
Searching files from parent folder
Untracked files are not copied
Helper scripts
BONUS: Visual Studio Code extensions
Intro
Do you know what is a git worktree? And if you do, do you actually use them at all?
If your answer is “no”, don’t worry: it’s the same for most developers out there.
That was also my case a couple of years ago, when I learned about git worktress completely by accident. But since then, they have become the base of my development workflow.
The fact that worktrees have been part of Git since 2015 makes it even more surprising that they remain so rarely known. But what if I told you…
You are already using worktrees
Even if you don’t know it!
Let’s see what is going on with a freshly cloned repo:
Yes, all git repos have a main worktree out of the box!
What is actually a worktree?
In fact it’s very simple:
a working tree is the same as a working directory
, this is, the directory with the files that you are working on.
That’s why the repo must have at least a main working tree, otherwise you would not be able to work with your files!
It helps to understand the structure of a git repo:
Original image by Zvonimir Spajic
OK, so then, what’s so special about worktrees?
Hmm… did you catch that? I wrote worktree
s
. Plural.
This is because a repository can actually have multiple working trees!
And most importantly,
each worktree can point to a different branch
.
Original image by GitKraken
This means switching between branches is as easy as switching between directories!
This unlocks a much better workflow when you have to juggle between multiple branches.
Worktree based workflow vs typical workflow
You are working on that cool new feature, when suddenly the alarms go blaring 🚨. Production is down! You have to deploy a hotfix, and you have to do it fast!
What would you usually do? Most likely something like:
Stage the changes of whatever you are working on (
git add .
)
Stash them (
git stash push
)
Checkout a new branch for the hotfix (
git checkout -b hotfix/my-fix
)
Do the fix
Stage, commit, push the changes
Phew! Now that the fire is out, you want to go back to the feature you left halfway, so you:
Checkout back to the branch you were working on (
git checkout feature/my-cool-feature
)
Pop the stash to recover your changes (
git stash pop
)
Finally keep working
With worktrees, you can instead switch between branches just by changing directories, without losing any of your work in the process, even if it’s not committed.
Let’s do the same hotfix, but this time using worktrees:
Create a new worktree (
git worktree add ../hotfix
)
cd
to the folder (
cd ../hotfix
)
Do the fix
Stage, commit, push the changes
cd
back to the worktree of the feature you were working on (
cd ../my-cool-feature
)
Keep working like if nothing happened.
That’s a bit better, isn’t it?
Worktrees allow us to have much more flexibility for many other day-to-day tasks:
🔍
Code reviews
: you can checkout the code and test it locally without disturbing your current work.
🔢
Maintaining different versions
of a codebase: you can have a worktree for each version, and switch between them easily.
🧶
Stuck on a rebase
and need to work on something else: you can leave it as is and just use another worktree.
🤺
Long-running tests or builds
: no need to wait for them to finish, just move to another worktree.
Source: xkcd
Sorry but this won’t be an excuse anymore
I’m sure by now you are already thinking of even more use cases :)
Worktrees commands
Luckily, the basic usage of worktrees is very simple. Just a few commands!
git worktree add [path] [branch]
creates a new worktree at the path specified, based on a given branch.
git worktree remove [path]
deletes a worktree. Keep in mind that this will delete the local folder, but the branch will still exist.
git worktree list
lists all the worktrees: useful to keep track of them when you have many.
Here is an example of using the different commands:
Better ways to work with worktrees
The previous example shows the most basic way to work with worktrees, but there are better ways.
But before we start:
How NOT to use worktrees
Do not create a worktree inside another worktree!
So never do
git worktree add new-worktree
from within a working directory (notice how there is no
../
).
This will create a new worktree inside the current worktree, which will be considered new content to be added to the repo… a total mess:
With that out of the way, let’s see the next level in using worktrees for your dev workflow.
Worktrees level 1: project folder
A better way t

data.title: If GLP-1 Drugs Are Good for Everything, Should We All Be on Them?
data.author: gamechangr
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了GLP-1药物（如Ozempic）的广泛功效。最初用于治疗肥胖和糖尿病，研究发现这些药物还能减少心脏病、癌症风险、偏头痛以及记忆丧失等。GLP-1药物似乎对多种疾病都有效，包括抑制成瘾行为、预防中风、心脏病、帕金森等，甚至缓解关节疼痛和减缓阿尔茨海默病的记忆衰退。然而，作者提醒，科学研究是一个逐步接近真相的过程，目前的发现仍需更多验证。虽然GLP-1药物展现出巨大潜力，但其最终效果尚需多年研究。因此，不应将其视为万能药。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GLP-1药物的科学性质、应用效果及伦理问题

不同观点：
• [andsoitis] 认为科学是一个不断探索、验证和推翻的过程，而不是永恒真理的集合。他指出GLP-1类药物的副作用对于健康人群来说不值得冒险，并提到其他抗炎药物如二甲双胍作为替代选择。

• [classichasclass] 分享了一个实际病例，展示了GLP-1药物在糖尿病患者管理中的成功应用，并通过个人经历说明了药物的具体效果，如体重减轻和A1c指标的改善。此外，他还对文章配图中的细节进行了指正。

• [falcor84] 对文章的写作表示赞赏，并表达了对GLP-1药物未来潜力的乐观看法，认为它可能会在未来被视为解码身体和人类健康的重大发现。

• [BryantD] 基于个人使用GLP-1药物的经验，指出药物在健康和体重控制方面的积极效果，但也提到药物对生活质量的负面影响，特别是对食物享受的减少。他表示对未来的研究进展保持关注。

• [ivape] 对GLP-1药物作为非医疗用途的昂贵“虚荣药物”提出质疑，认为即使通过一些手段获得药物，其高昂的费用也让人难以承受。

补充讨论：
• GLP-1药物的实际应用效果在不同患者中存在差异，既有成功的医疗案例，也有对生活质量影响的担忧。
• 药物的可及性和费用问题引发了关于其作为非医疗用途的伦理讨论。
• 科学的本质及其在药物研发和应用中的角色成为讨论的重要主题，强调了科学作为探索过程而非绝对真理的集合。

争议焦点：GLP-1药物对于健康人群的适用性和费用问题，以及其在改善健康和生活质量之间的平衡。

Several years ago, scientists took a close look at GLP-1 drugs, such as Ozempic, and learned that they were good at helping people lose weight. Then they took an even closer look and learned the drugs are also good at just about everything else.
GLP-1s—technically known as glucagon like peptide 1 receptor agonists—seem to curb alcohol, cocaine, and tobacco use among addicts. They
prevent
strokes, heart attacks, chronic kidney disease, sleep apnea, and Parkinson's disease. They’re associated with
a lower risk
of several cancers, including pancreatic cancer and multiple myeloma. Arthritic patients on the drugs
experienced
relief from knee pain that was “on par with opioid drugs.” A small study
found
that they reduce migraine headaches by 50 percent. And emerging research suggests they might even slow the rate of memory loss among people diagnosed with Alzheimer’s.

I know that this must sound completely absurd. I barely believe it, myself. Life elixirs and holy grails belong in fantasy novels and Indiana Jones movies. Any reasonably skeptical person confronting this extraordinary list of effects must have several questions screaming to the front of their mind, including but not limited to:
Are we sure GLP-1 drugs are this good?
How can one drug do everything?
If the drugs really do everything, why aren’t we all on it?
This post is my effort to answer all three questions.
But first, a word of caution. Some people think of Science, with a capital-“S”, as the official declaration of eternal truths. I prefer to think of science, with a lower-case “s”, as a messy scrabble toward half-truths that are often overturned with further research. I’m thrilled by studies that make GLP-1 therapies seem like holy water drawn from the fountain of youth. I’m also a realist who suspects that the final verdict on this medicine is many years away. So, please think of this as a first draft of history as we know it, rather than some kind of official announcement that GLP-1 drugs should be piped into the municipal water supply.
1. Are we sure GLP-1 drugs are this good?
As a fixture in news headlines, GLP-1 drugs are a recent phenomenon. As a subject of scientific study, however, the molecule is decades in the making.
Our story begins with a deep-sea monster. In the 1970s, a team of genetics researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital were studying animal hormones when they ran into a problem. The National Institutes of Health
had banned
some gene editing in warm-blooded animals on ethical grounds. So, the scientists went looking for cold-blooded animals instead. They settled on the anglerfish—which resembles the physical manifestation of a Tim Burton nightmare—because, as one scientist put it, they’re "a trash fish ... they’re ugly.” Tragically, no one at NIH was clamoring to protect this handsome fella:
Scrutinizing the poor beast, the scientists had a “eureka moment” when they
discovered
that anglerfish genes coded for several peptides related to the gut hormone glucagon. Scientists later identified that hormone as “glucagon-like peptide 1”—GLP-1. Further research showed that GLP-1 reduced blood sugar levels in mammals, making it a promising candidate for diabetes medication. The problem, however, was that the molecule’s half-life was much too short to serve as a useful medicine.
Enter the lizard. In the early 1990s, the scientist John Eng wanted to understand how the Gila monster, the stocky venomous reptile pictured below, could survive for several months between meals. When he studied the lizard’s venom, he discovered that its saliva contained a hormone called exendin-4, which worked much the same way as GLP-1, but lasted much longer.
A drug based on that molecule, called Exenatide, became the first approved GLP-1 receptor agonist for treating diabetes in 2005. This breakthrough kicked off an arms race. In 2010, the Danish company Novo Nordisk received regulatory approval for their drug liraglutide. In 2017, the FDA approved another drug, semaglutide, which is the basis for Ozempic and Wegovy. As the chart below shows, the arms race is accelerating. In the last few years, scientists have found that targeting multiple gut-hormones leads to even greater weight loss.

Analysis
Alberta no longer sure about big savings from auto insurance reforms
Danielle Smith said the new system would cut premiums by up to $400. But rising insurance costs, hail storms and tariffs are putting that claim in doubt.
Due to tariffs, hail storms, UCP moving off prediction of $400 premium reduction
Jason Markusoff
·
CBC News
·
Posted: Aug 07, 2025 2:16 PM EDT | Last Updated: 6 hours ago
A 2014 car crash in Edmonton that hurt five people. In 2027, Alberta will move to an insurance system that greatly restricts ability to sue for damages after automobile collisions, with the expectation that will help curb premium increases.
(CBC)
Social Sharing
When Premier Danielle Smith announced a dramatic shift to a new auto insurance system that largely removes Albertans' rights to sue at-fault drivers for compensation, she and her ministers dangled the prospect of big discounts for motorists.
"These better, faster services would be delivered at a savings of up to $400 per year on insurance premiums," she said at the November announcement.
Standing behind a lectern that said "keeping Alberta affordable," Smith outlined major reforms to a system that has remained the second-most expensive among all Canadian provinces.
The $400 figure, taken from an expert report on insurance reforms, has kept popping up in UCP government messages since then, including in a
promotional video
released in April. It repeated the claim alongside an image of a woman looking at her laptop and smiling wide, as the outline of a piggy bank appeared over her head. "It's better for your wallet, and if you're injured in an accident, it's better for your health," the voiceover actor stated.
Alberta's promotional video on its insurance reforms, released in April, highlighted the prospect of $400 in savings. The government has now distanced itself from that figure.
(Government of Alberta/YouTube)
But in a government report released Aug.6 that's full of details on how auto insurance will work when the new system arrives in 2027, $400 in savings never gets mentioned. Nor do any claims or suggestions about how much, exactly, driver premiums will drop by, thanks to this big overhaul.
An Alberta Finance official stated earlier this week that the initial $400 cost savings figure was devised using 2023 insurance data. Various pressures have since pushed up the cost of providing insurance, ranging from inflation to U.S. tariffs on steel and car parts, to Calgary's hail storms and the Jasper wildfire. The government will perform additional actuarial analysis to help better predict the pricing impact of the new model, the official said.
Finance Minister Nate Horner offered a new explanation about the savings claim he and Smith made last fall.
He pointed to the fact Alberta has capped this year's premium hikes for good drivers at 7.5 per cent this year, while the
government estimate
that private insurers lost money on auto coverage last year, to the tune of 19.6 per cent. The rate cap is now keeping rates "artificially low," the minister said Wednesday.
"I would look at it this way, and this is where it's tough to communicate: they may already be seeing a $400 per premium savings due to the good driver rate cap," Horner told CBC News in an interview. In other words, without the rate cap insurers might have charged Albertans around $2,100 a year instead of the $1,703 average premiums they now pay, the minister is reasoning.
Smith and Horner first floated the $400 savings last fall in conjunction with letting insurers hike rates this year by up to 7.5-per-cent rate and 7.5 per cent in 2026 as well — pending review — after past years of lower caps and rate freezes.
Given how "fragile" the system is now thanks to cost woes, Horner said, he would not commit to keeping next year's hike at 7.5 per cent, saying it will depend on a statistical analysis.
"I promised the Premier and Cabinet that I will bring something forward this fall for their consideration… I can't tell you what will come out of that."
"Affordable" was the watchword when Premier Danielle Smith announced Alberta's largest insurance reforms in decades last November. Affordability and Utilities Minister Nathan Neudorf is at left and Finance Minister Nate Horner at right.
(Dave Bajer/CBC)
The insurance sector wants the rate cap lifted, and has begun making similar warnings that big savings will not materialize come 2027 through Alberta's insurance system redesign.
Aaron Sutherland, a vice-president with the Insurance Bureau of Canada, not only highlighted the tariffs and climate disasters — he also cited the government's promises this new system will offer Canada's richest benefits for the injured and also preserve more ability to sue than other provinces with "no-fault" insurance systems.

data.title: Echelon kills smart home gym equipment offline capabilities with update
data.author: akyuu
data.article_summary: Echelon智能家用健身设备在一次固件更新后，强制要求连接其服务器才能正常工作，导致未联网的设备失去关键功能。更新后，设备需要与Echelon服务器进行"握手"获取解锁密钥，否则将完全无法使用，甚至无法进行手动锻炼或蓝牙连接。这导致依赖第三方应用QZ（连接Echelon设备与Peloton、Strava等平台）的用户无法同步数据。Echelon通过此举可能旨在推动用户使用其订阅服务，以增加收入和数据收集。然而，这引发了用户不满，尤其是在设备离线时无法使用。开发者Viola呼吁Echelon允许设备在无网络情况下通过加密方式连接其他设备。

A firmware update has killed key functionality for Echelon smart home gym equipment that isn't connected to the Internet.
As explained in a Tuesday
blog post
by Roberto Viola, who develops the "QZ (qdomyos-zwift)"
app
that connects Echelon machines to third-party fitness platforms, like Peloton, Strava, and Apple HealthKit, the firmware update forces Echelon machines to connect to Echelon’s servers in order to work properly. A user online
reported
that as a result of updating his machine, it is no longer syncing with apps like QZ, and he is unable to view his machine's exercise metrics in the Echelon app without an Internet connection.
Affected Echelon machines reportedly only have full functionality, including the ability to share real-time metrics, if a user has the Echelon app active and if the machine is able to reach Echelon’s servers. Viola wrote:
On startup, the device must
log in to Echelon’s servers
.
The server sends back a temporary, rotating unlock key.
Without this handshake, the device is
completely bricked
—no manual workout, no Bluetooth pairing, no nothing.
Because updated Echelon machines now require a connection to Echelon servers for some basic functionality, users are unable to use their equipment and understand, for example, how fast they're going without an Internet connection. If Echelon were to ever
go out of business
, the gym equipment would, essentially, get bricked.
Viola told Ars Technica that he first started hearing about problems with QZ, which launched in 2020, at the end of 2024 from treadmill owners. He said a firmware update appears to have rolled out this month on Echelon bikes that bricks QZ functionality. Echelon didn’t respond to Ars Technica’s request for comment.
In his blog, Viola urged Echelon to let its machines send encrypted data to another device, like a phone or a tablet, without the Internet. He wrote:
Users bought the bike; they should be allowed to use it with or without Echelon’s services.
Echelon is in hardware, software, and subscription sales, which makes independently running equipment and apps like QZ potential threats. Yet, it's still vexing to see another example of a company
changing the capabilities
of its products after people already bought them. Not all Echelon owners use QZ, but many owners may be impacted when the machines lose key functionality if offline.
Some might never have purchased Echelon equipment if they knew the machines might one day fail to work without a web connection or Echelon account.
Third-party app connections severed
For
some owners
of Echelon equipment, QZ, which is currently rated as the
No. 9
sports app on Apple's App Store, has been central to their workouts. QZ connects the equipment to platforms like Zwift, which shows people virtual, scenic worlds while they’re exercising. It has also enabled new features for some machines, like automatic resistance adjustments. Because of this, Viola argued in his blog that QZ has "helped companies grow."
“A large reason I got the [E]chelon was because of your app and I have put thousands of miles on the bike since 2021,” a Reddit user
told
the developer on the social media platform on Wednesday.
However, Echelon’s firmware update likely seeks to regain some of the revenue opportunities that overlap with the capabilities that apps like QZ enable. Echelon's subscription-based app, which starts at $40 per month, also offers "guided scenic rides,” for example. QZ can allow people to watch Peloton classes from their Echelon device, but Echelon
sells its own
fitness classes. The Tennessee-headquartered company has been
investing
in ways to get customers more engaged with its
personalized workout platform, too
, which requires the machines to be online.
There’s also value in customer data. Getting more customers to exercise with its app means Echelon may gather more data for things like feature development and marketing.
Echelon is a private company, and we don’t know how much money it is making, but it’s likely that its financial goals hinge on subscription sales, which can generate more revenue than expensive equipment purchases. Meanwhile, Echelon is competing with other tech-centric companies offering gym equipment and classes,
like the Peloton
.
Viola runs QZ, which costs $7 to $8 to download, alone, offering users a lot of support via online communities. He told Ars that revenue from app purchases covers his costs “more or less.”
"It was never my intention to damage anyone’s business. This is just competition. The best product should prevail," Viola said. "I never created QZ to get rich; I just wanted users to have a great hour of fitness when they choose, without connection issues, subscriptions, or [other limitations]."

data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了《旧学校》（Old School）游戏在玩家数量激增的背景下，对游戏世界的需求大增。为了满足需求，Jagex在过去三周内新增了43个世界，并计划再增加20个美国世界。然而，增加新世界并非简单地添加服务器，背后有复杂的基础设施需要升级。文章提到，他们正在升级基础设施以提升容量，并计划推出云托管世界，首先从美国东海岸开始，以实现更好的扩展和未来proof的服务器架构。云托管还将帮助他们更快地进入新地区，如南美和东南亚。文章还简要介绍了当前游戏世界的托管方式，使用虚拟机和VMWare vSphere等技术，并强调需要平衡虚拟CPU和物理CPU的比例以确保性能。

44830917.article_content:
More Worlds, More Power: The Road To Greater Capacity
07 August 2025
If you've been delving deep, roaming the lands, or standing in a crowded GE recently, youve probably noticed that Old School is more alive than ever. The Platinum Age is real, and we couldnt be more thrilled.
With so many new and returning players joining the fun, demand for game worlds has skyrocketed. We're working hard behind the scenes to meet that demand, and today we want to update you again on whats been done, whats coming next, and why this isnt just a simple case of "add more servers lol".
Weve recently spun up a whole bunch of
new worlds
(an additional 43 in the last three weeks) across the US, UK, Germany, and Australia, with more on the way! But heres the catch: Throwing new worlds online isnt quite as straightforward as it might seem.
Behind each game world is a complex infrastructure, and if we just keep stacking on more without addressing the underlying systems, we risk creating performance issues, lag, and instability across the board. Thats obviously not something were okay with! So, what are we doing about it?
Were continuing to roll out new worlds as player demand continues to rise. These will be added in a staggered fashion to help us monitor performance and avoid overloading our current capacity. Next week we're aiming to add an additional 20 US worlds!
Were upgrading our infrastructure to remove limits and give more breathing room to each world. Work is ongoing and progress is accelerating towards being complete!
Were launching cloud-hosted worlds, starting with US East Coast, to offer better scaling and future-proof our server architecture. We're aiming to have this done within the next month.
What This Means for Regional Servers
Once our cloud-based hosting is running smoothly, itll unlock something players have been asking about for a long time: regional servers in new territories.
Rather than relying on physical hardware in every corner of the world (front-loaded capital expense, logistically tricky), this shift lets us scale into new regions without setting up shop from scratch. That means were one step closer to supporting players in regions like South America, Southeast Asia, or beyond.
Were not quite there yet, and each new location will still require some bespoke work, but we hear you, and were building towards it!
If all you're interested in is a quick TLDR; then this is where you can stop reading. If you're interested in learning more about our server infrastructure, keep on scrolling...
Spudworks: What Powers Your Game World?
At this point we turn to our wonderful Spudworks from the infrastructure team who can peel back the layers behind our worlds much better than anyone else!
If you're unable to see the image above,
click here!
With great player counts come great server responsibilities, and the hamsters are working overtime. Let's quickly explore how OSRS Worlds are currently hosted, what we are working on in the immediate term to provide more capacity, and steps we are taking to make our World hosting capacity more elastic going forward.
Being a Spudworks post, therell be a bit of tech-jargon to deal with and - as we in the Infrastructure Team are such a utilitarian bunch - graphs and diagrams lifted directly from internal sources, but we'll do our best to explain as we go. Lets get started!
Hosting an OSRS World
We'll start with how Jagex hosts OSRS Worlds today. There are often comments speculating about this so let's take a peek.
Game worlds are run on virtual machines (multiple software-defined computers within a single physical computer, known as a Hypervisor). These virtual machines are hosted in regional commercial Data Centres to reduce latency between the Worlds and you lovely lot.
Public Cloud, in our case Amazon Web Services, is deployed at Jagex, but right now its use is confined to our core infrastructure, which provides global services such as the Jagex Accounts system, Player Saves, and data analytics.
If you're unable to see the image above,
click here!
Jagex-ey Royals
For those interested, here's a very quick look at our hypervisors:
We employ 4Ghz Intel CPUs. These are reasonably high-frequency for server grade CPUs, where there are trade-offs between single core performance, overall core density, and thermal output.
We run VMWare vSphere with Linux Virtual Machines but may move away from VMWare in future.
Providing more Worlds
More players, more worlds!
We hear you! As much as wed love to simply double the World count, things get... complicated.
While we have some head room in our Edge Tier, adding a large number of new Worlds will increase the ratio of Virtual CPUs to Physical CPUs. Allocating more Virtual CPUs than you have Physical CPUs is called overcommitting and, while common in virtualised environments, pushing this ratio too high will impact World performance as many busy Virtual Machines compete for execution on a finite pool of physical CPUs.

data.author: lackoftactics

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[GPT-OSS模型的性能、本地运行能力、技术架构及其对开源AI生态的影响]

不同观点：
• [对GPT-OSS模型的性能表示惊叹]
  - gpt-oss:20b在MMLU上排名前十，接近Gemini-2.5-Pro。
  - 可以在Macbook Air M3等消费级设备上本地运行，成本极低。
  - 20B模型的性能接近o3-mini，120B模型接近o4。

• [对技术架构的评价]
  - 使用了标准的Grouped-Query Attention和MoE架构，没有采用Deepseek等的最新改进。
  - 量化技术（MXFP4格式）是亮点，但与其他开源量化方案（如Unsloth的1.58bit）相比并无显著优势。
  - 推理部分使用Rust编写（如harmony和tiktoken），显示OpenAI对Rust的偏好。

• [对开源策略的讨论]
  - 开源模型长期来看会获胜，中国公司的快速迭代证明了这一点。
  - OpenAI此次开源可能是为了抢占市场，同时保留最新技术。
  - 开源N-1代模型可以捕获潜在价值并加速下一代开发。

• [对本地运行的体验]
  - 使用Ollama等工具可以轻松运行模型，体验良好。
  - 但预填充时间较长，影响了工具使用的效率。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点：GPT-OSS的技术架构是否足够先进，还是OpenAI保留了更先进的技术。
- 其他值得注意的点：模型的安全性和信任基准测试，以及如何在Mac设备上优化运行（如使用MLX）。

data.title: The US Economy Was Supposed to Be in a Recession by Now. What Happened?
data.author: gamechangr
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了本应陷入衰退的美国经济为何至今仍表现良好。尽管特朗普政府的关税政策最初遭到广泛批评，且许多经济学家预测这将导致经济灾难，但截至2025年7月，美国经济表现出人意料地稳定。股市创下新高，消费者信心和零售销售均好于预期，通胀也未如预测般飙升。文章指出，许多宣布的关税并未真正实施或被推迟，政策变化频繁，使得实际影响难以评估。尽管关税政策不利于经济，但美国经济体量庞大，具有韧性，短期内未显现严重负面影响。文章呼吁对特朗普经济政策保持批判性思考，同时承认当前经济的意外 resilience。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对经济衰退的预测及当前经济形势的分析

不同观点：
• [paxys] 认为经济学家的预测并不总是准确，他们准确预测了过去两次经济衰退中的14次。这暗示了对经济衰退预测的不可靠性，有讽刺意味。

• [fuzzfactor] 提出当前经济可能正在进入衰退，但按照时间推算，尚未到能够被测量的程度。同时，对Navarro的采访让他意识到问题的存在。"Ungenuine"这个词被质疑其正确性，可能是在讨论言辞的真实性。

• [igor47] 将当前形势与特朗普时期进行类比，认为特朗普时期很多政策因下属的干预而未能完全实施，并被用来证明特朗普政策并不糟糕。他预测关税政策也会如此，公众难以理解细微差别和长期影响，且会把其他事件当作经济衰退的原因，如爱泼斯坦事件或将责任归咎于奥巴马。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于对经济衰退的预测和判断的准确性，以及如何解读和归因经济现象。
• [fuzzfactor] 对"ungenuine"一词的使用反映了对言辞真实性的关注。
• [igor47] 提到公众在理解复杂经济现象和政策影响方面的困难，暗示了对政治和经济讨论中误导信息的担忧。
• 整体讨论反映出对当前经济形势和政策影响的困惑和多重解读。

The US Economy Was Supposed to Be in a Recession By Now. What Happened?
Poisoned by inflation, shot by tariffs, counted out by economists, it just keeps kicking.
Derek Thompson
Jul 25, 2025
458

The US Economy Was Supposed to Be in a Recession By Now. What Happened?
Copy link

More
73
